paras.en: Since, then, Christ deigned to die for the ungodly, it is rightly added: [[5:8|But God commendeth his charity towards us|Commendat autem caritatem suam Deus in nobis]], that is, God the Father, or the Trinity, shows it to be commendable or praiseworthy, his charity, that is, which he has toward us and by which he loves us, through the effect of his surpassing mercy; [[5:8|because when as yet we were sinners|quoniam quum adhuc peccatores essemus]], that is, subject to the yoke of the vices, entangled in the bonds of sins, and not redeemed from original sin, [[5:8|according to the time|secundum tempus]] that went before Christ's Passion, that is, before Christ died for us. For the Apostle speaks in the person of the human race, many of whose members went before the time of Christ's Passion: and they were then, in whose person the Apostle says this. Or, *according to the time*, that is, for the three [days …] [a line is missing from the transcription here] [[5:9|Christ died for us|Christus pro nobis mortuus est]], that is, deigned to die, that, [[1 Pet 3:18|being put to death indeed in the flesh, but enlivened in the spirit|mortificati carne, vivificatique spiritu]] [Denis applies the words to us: "mortified in the flesh and quickened in the spirit"], we may serve him [[Luke 1:75|In holiness and justice|in sanctitate atque justitia]][[Luke 1:74||]]. In which shines out the inestimable charity of God the Father toward us, according to that word of John: [[John 3:16|God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son|Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret]]. And the Apostle: [[Eph 2:4|for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us|Propter nimiam, inquit, caritatem suam qua dilexit nos]], he says, God the Father sent his Son[[Gal 4:4||]]. [[5:9|Much more therefore, being now justified by his blood|Multo igitur magis justificati nunc in sanguine ipsius]], that is, since Christ died for us when we were still wicked, weak and sinners, much more now, our reconciliation and freeing having been accomplished, being justified, that is, cleansed from the vices and having obtained grace by the shedding of Christ's blood, [[5:9|shall we be saved from wrath|salvi erimus ab ira]], that is, from eternal damnation, [[5:9|through him|per ipsum]], namely Christ, or by his merit. For it is more to justify the ungodly than to rescue the justified from punishment.

paras.t: Si, pro quia, enim quum inimici essemus, id est Deo propter iniquitatem odibiles, rebelles, et natura filii iræ, etiam propter peccatum originale, reconciliati sumus Deo, id est ad ejus amicitiam revocati, deleta videlicet causa inimicitiæ, puta peccato, per mortem Filii ejus; multo magis reconciliati jam salvi erimus, non solum ab ira prædicta, sed etiam consequendo vitam æternam, in vita ipsius, id est per gloriosam vitam Christi, seu virtute Christi glorificati. Si enim potuit per suam mortem nos justificare, certissimum est quod jam vivens possit nos beatificare, præsertim quum unum ordinetur ad aliud, scilicet justificatio ad beatificationem.
paras.en: [[5:10|For if|Si enim]] (*if* standing for *since*) [[5:10|when we were enemies|quum inimici essemus]], that is, hateful to God because of iniquity, rebels, and [[Eph 2:3|by nature children of wrath|natura filii iræ]], on account of original sin as well, [[5:10|we were reconciled to God|reconciliati sumus Deo]], that is, called back to his friendship, the cause of enmity, namely sin, having been blotted out, [[5:10|by the death of his Son|per mortem Filii ejus]]; [[5:10|much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved|multo magis reconciliati jam salvi erimus]], not only from the wrath spoken of, but also by gaining eternal life, [[5:10|by his life|in vita ipsius]], that is, through the glorious life of Christ, or by the power of the glorified Christ. For if he could justify us by his death, it is most certain that, now living, he can beatify us, especially since the one is ordered to the other, namely justification to beatification.

paras.t: Quæri potest, quum Dei dilectio sit invariabilis et æterna, quomodo dicimur Deo reconciliari, et quomodo eramus ejus inimici, et postmodum facti sumus amici. Et respondendum, quod Deus omnes electos ante mundi constitutionem dilexit, eosque immutabiliter diligit, secundum rationem prædestinationis divinæ, non autem secundum rationem præsentis justitiæ. Dicimur ergo Deo reconciliari per Christum, in quantum per ejus passionem ablata nobis est culpa, per quam displicuimus Deo secundum rationem et ordinem suæ justitiæ ad nos comparatæ. Vel respondendum, quod Deus invariabiliter diligit electos per respectum ad bonum gratiæ et gloriæ quod eis dare disposuit. Odit autem eos quantum ad culpam, juxta illud: Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem. Et ita dicuntur ei reconciliari, quum culpa aufertur, et pœna finitur. Unde Sapiens dicit: Diligis, Domine, omnia quæ sunt, et nihil odisti eorum quæ fecisti. Idem ipse ait et alibi quoque: Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus. Hæc enim atque similia nullam mutationem ponunt in Deo, sed in creatura, quæ ad Creatorem aliter et aliter se habet.
paras.en: It may be asked, since God's love is unchangeable and eternal, how we are said to be reconciled to God, and how we were his enemies and afterwards were made friends. The answer is that God loved all the elect before the foundation of the world[[Eph 1:4||]], and loves them unchangeably, by reason of the divine predestination, but not by reason of present justice. We are said, then, to be reconciled to God through Christ inasmuch as through his Passion the guilt was taken from us by which we displeased God according to the reckoning and order of his justice as it stands toward us. Or the answer is that God loves the elect unchangeably with regard to the good of grace and glory which he has determined to give them; but he hates them as to their guilt, according to that word: [[Ps 5:7|Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity|Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem]]. And so they are said to be reconciled to him when the guilt is taken away and the punishment ended. Hence the Wise man says: [[Wis 11:25|For thou lovest all things that are, and hatest none of the things which thou hast made|Diligis, Domine, omnia quæ sunt, et nihil odisti eorum quæ fecisti]]. And the same says elsewhere too: [[Wis 14:9|But to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful alike|Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]]. For these and like sayings place no change in God, but in the creature, which stands now in one way, now in another, toward the Creator.

paras.t: Non solum autem hoc modo salvi erimus in futuro, sed et gloriamur in Deo, id est, nunc quoque in præsenti exsilio exsultamus per spem in Deo, id est in contemplatione ac dilectione ipsius, gaudentes de hoc, quod tandem aliquando videre eum speramus per speciem. Et ita futuram jucunditatem et gloriam in præsenti peregrinatione quodammodo inchoamus. Gloriamur autem in Deo, per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui est nobis via et ostium accedendi ad Deum, cujus etiam merito datur nobis gloriatio ista: et ex consideratione passionis suæ et aliorum beneficiorum speramus et exsultamus in Deo, qui tanta nobis per Christum largitus est; per quem nunc, id est tempore gratiæ, reconciliationem cum Deo accepimus.
paras.en: [[5:11|And not only so|Non solum autem]] shall we be saved in this way in the future, [[5:11|but also we glory in God|sed et gloriamur in Deo]], that is, even now in this present exile we exult through hope in God, that is, in contemplating and loving him, rejoicing in this, that we hope at last some day to see him face to face. And so in our present pilgrimage we in some way begin the joy and glory to come. And we glory in God [[5:11|through our Lord Jesus Christ|per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]], who is for us the way and [[John 10:9|the door|ostium]] of drawing near to God, by whose merit too this glorying is given us: and from considering his Passion and his other benefits we hope and exult in God, who has bestowed such great things on us through Christ; [[5:11|by whom we have now received reconciliation|per quem nunc reconciliationem accepimus]], *now*, that is, in the time of grace, reconciliation with God.

paras.t: Propterea, sicut per unum hominem, scilicet Adam, primum nostrum parentem, peccatum originale in hunc mundum, id est in homines in mundo hoc habitantes, intravit, et per peccatum mors corporalis, quæ consecuta est culpam. Quamvis enim mors sit naturalis homini, considerando naturam corporis sui ex contrariis compositam, tamen si non peccasset, mortem non incurrisset, ex dono gratiæ seu virtute originalis justitiæ. Et sic considerando supernaturalem institutionem hominis, mors culpam secuta est, non naturam. Et ita in omnes homines mors pertransiit. Sicut enim omnes nati sunt sine originali justitia, sic etiam immortalitate justitiam illam concomitante privantur. In quo uno homine, scilicet Adam, omnes peccaverunt, non actualiter, sed virtualiter, originale peccatum incurrendo: quod eis imputatur in culpam, in quantum aliquo modo erant in primo parente, et idem cum ipso. Erant autem in ipso sicut in primo principio generationis humanæ. Et sicut multa membra sunt in uno corpore, et multa individua in una specie, sic quodammodo omnes eramus in primo parente secundum corpulentam substantiam, seu materialem propagationem. Porro originalis justitia sic data erat primo parenti, ut transfunderetur in posteros. Ideo primo parente hac justitia destituto, posteri ejus juste privantur eadem: nec tamen fit eis injuria, quia nec primo parenti, nec eis ista justitia naturaliter debebatur aut competebat, sed nec beatifica visio Dei, qua merebantur privari propter hujus justitiæ privationem. Ab eo autem quod dicitur, In quo omnes peccaverunt, excipiendus est Christus homo, qui non naturali ordine aut per concupiscentiam genitus est.
paras.en: [[5:12|Wherefore as by one man|Propterea, sicut per unum hominem]], namely Adam, our first parent, [[5:12|sin entered into this world|peccatum in hunc mundum intravit]], original sin, into this world, that is, into the men who dwell in this world, [[5:12|and by sin death|et per peccatum mors]], bodily death, which followed upon guilt. For although death is natural to man, if we consider the nature of his body, composed of contraries, yet had he not sinned he would not have incurred death, by the gift of grace or the power of original justice. And so, considering the supernatural establishment of man, death followed guilt, not nature. [[5:12|And so death passed upon all men|Et ita in omnes homines mors pertransiit]]. For as all are born without original justice, so they are also deprived of the immortality that went with that justice. [[5:12|In whom|In quo]], in which one man, namely Adam, [[5:12|all have sinned|omnes peccaverunt]], not actually but virtually, by incurring original sin: which is imputed to them as guilt inasmuch as they were in some way in the first parent, and one with him. And they were in him as in the first principle of human generation. And as many members are in one body, and many individuals in one species, so in a manner we were all in the first parent according to bodily substance, or material propagation. Further, original justice was so given to the first parent that it should be passed on to his descendants. Therefore, the first parent having been stripped of this justice, his descendants are justly deprived of it: yet no injury is done them, since this justice was not naturally due to, nor belonged to, either the first parent or them; nor was the beatific vision of God, of which they deserved to be deprived on account of the privation of this justice. But from what is said, *in whom all have sinned*, Christ as man is to be excepted, who was not begotten in the natural order or through concupiscence.

paras.t: Merito autem dixi omnes peccasse in uno. Usque ad legem scriptam, id est usque ad dationem legis Mosaicæ, scilicet a principio mundi, quando non erat nisi lex naturalis, peccatum erat in mundo, in genere humano, tam originale quam actuale. Vel, Usque ad legem scriptam inclusive, peccatum erat in mundo, quia lex Moysis peccatum auferre non potuit sicut lex gratiæ. Propter quod aiebat Apostolus ad Judæos: Per Jesum remissio peccatorum annuntiatur vobis, in omnibus a quibus non potuistis in lege Moysis justificari. […] batur, quum lex non esset. Hæc Augustinus et alii ita exponunt: Peccatum quodcumque non imputabatur, id est, ignorabatur, nec peccatum esse reputabatur ab hominibus excæcatis, in quibus ratio naturalis fuerat vitiis obfuscata: imputabatur tamen a Deo. Videtur autem posse exponi hoc modo, quod peccatum non imputabatur a Deo hominibus, non quod penitus non imputabatur, sed quia non imputabatur tam graviter, quum lex scripta non esset. Erat enim tunc magis excusabile quam post legislationem. Juxta quem sensum in præcedenti capitulo dixit Apostolus: Ubi non est lex, nec prævaricatio.
paras.en: And rightly did I say that all sinned in one. [[5:13|For until the law|Usque ad legem]], the written law, that is, until the giving of the law of Moses, namely from the beginning of the world, when there was only the natural law, [[5:13|sin was in the world|peccatum erat in mundo]], in the human race, both original and actual. Or, *until the law*, the written law, inclusively, *sin was in the world*, since the law of Moses could not take away sin[[Heb 10:4||]] as the law of grace can. For which reason the Apostle said to the Jews: [[Acts 13:38|through him forgiveness of sins is preached to you: and from all the things from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses|Per Jesum remissio peccatorum annuntiatur vobis, in omnibus a quibus non potuistis in lege Moysis justificari]]. […] [some lines are missing from the transcription here; the text resumes in the middle of the lemma *but sin was not imputed*] [[5:13|when the law was not|quum lex non esset]]. Augustine and others explain these words thus: any sin *was not imputed*, that is, was not known, nor reckoned to be sin, by blinded men, in whom natural reason had been darkened by the vices: yet it was imputed by God. But it seems that it can be explained in this way: that sin was not imputed to men by God, not that it was not imputed at all, but that it was not imputed so gravely, *when the written law was not*. For it was then more excusable than after the giving of the law. In which sense the Apostle said in the preceding chapter: [[Rom 4:15|where there is no law, neither is there transgression|Ubi non est lex, nec prævaricatio]].

paras.t: Sed regnavit, id est prævaluit, mors corporalis; vel, mors culpæ originalis, quæ est ipsa carentia originalis justitiæ debitæ inesse; vel, mors limbi infernalis, quæ dici potest dilatio vitæ beatæ, atque detentio in lacu gehennæ; ab Adam usque ad Moysen inclusive, videlicet quousque Christus advenit, id est, tam tempore legis naturalis quam Mosaicæ; etiam in eos qui non peccaverunt peccato actuali, seu propria voluntate, ut sunt parvuli ante annos discretionis defuncti; vel, In eos qui non peccaverunt mortaliter, si qui tales fuerunt, ut sanctificati in utero, scilicet Jeremias, etc. Omnes enim hi propter reatum originalis peccati mortem corporalem pertulerunt, atque in limbo tenebantur, donec pro ipsis Christus satisfecit, liberando eos ab originalis culpæ reatu. Magis vero regnavit mors ante Moysen quam post. Per legem enim Moysis multi retrahebantur a morte culpæ, cœperuntque cognoscere vitam post hanc vitam, et resurrectionem futuram, et ita mortem temporalem minus quam ante timebant. Porro, Salvator regnum mortis destruxit, et suæ passionis exemplo nos contra mortis timorem armavit, ipsamque mortem temporalem, æternæ vitæ constituit januam. Propter quod ait per Prophetam: De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos: ero mors tua, o mors; morsus tuus ero, inferne. Et Apostolus: Ut per mortem liberaret eos qui per totam vitam timore mortis erant obnoxii servituti.
paras.en: [[5:14|But death reigned|Sed regnavit mors]], that is, prevailed, bodily death; or the death of original guilt, which is the very lack of the original justice that ought to be present; or the death of the limbo of hell, which can be called the putting off of the life of bliss and detention in the pit of hell; [[5:14|from Adam unto Moses|ab Adam usque ad Moysen]], inclusively, namely until Christ came, that is, both in the time of the natural law and in that of the law of Moses; [[5:14|even over them also who have not sinned|etiam in eos qui non peccaverunt]] by actual sin, or by their own will, as are little ones who died before the years of discretion; or, over those who have not sinned mortally, if there were any such, as those sanctified in the womb, namely Jeremias[[Jer 1:5||]], etc. For all these, because of the guilt of original sin, suffered bodily death and were held in limbo, until Christ made satisfaction for them, freeing them from the guilt of original sin. But death reigned more before Moses than after. For by the law of Moses many were drawn back from the death of guilt, and began to know of a life after this life and of the resurrection to come, and so feared temporal death less than before. Further, the Saviour destroyed the reign of death[[2 Tim 1:10||]][[Heb 2:14||]], and by the example of his Passion armed us against the fear of death, and made temporal death itself the gate of eternal life. For which reason he says through the Prophet: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos: ero mors tua, o mors; morsus tuus ero, inferne]]. And the Apostle: [[Heb 2:14|that, through death|Ut per mortem]], [[Heb 2:15|And might deliver them, who through the fear of death were all their lifetime subject to servitude|liberaret eos qui per totam vitam timore mortis erant obnoxii servituti]].

paras.t: Sic ergo regnavit mors in eos qui non peccaverunt, in similitudinem prævaricationis Adæ, id est propter assimilationem originalis culpæ, qua similes Adæ fuerunt. Quæ utique originalis culpa, erat in Adam prævaricatio actualis. Qui, scilicet Adam, est forma futuri, id est figura Christi, qui tempore Adæ erat venturus ut judicaretur in mundo, nunc vero venturus est ut judicet mundum. Dicitur autem Adam figura Christi: quoniam sicut Adam est principium omnium hominum quantum ad propagationem ac esse naturæ, sic Christus quantum ad infusionem gratiæ seu esse spirituale. Secundo, quoniam sicut Adam formatus est de limo terræ supernaturali virtute ac ordine, sic Christus natus est de Virgine Spiritus Sancti obumbratione. Item, sicut de latere Adæ dormientis sublata est costa unde formata est Eva, ita de latere Christi morientis fluxerunt sacramenta, quibus formatur Ecclesia. Sed hæc causa ad primam reducitur.
paras.en: So, then, death reigned over them who have not sinned, [[5:14|after the similitude of the transgression of Adam|in similitudinem prævaricationis Adæ]], that is, because of the likeness of original guilt, by which they were like Adam. Which original guilt was, in Adam, an actual transgression. [[5:14|Who|Qui]], namely Adam, [[5:14|is a figure of him who was to come|est forma futuri]], that is, a figure of Christ, who in Adam's time was to come to be judged in the world, but now is to come to judge the world. Adam is called a figure of Christ because, as Adam is the principle of all men as to propagation and the being of nature, so is Christ as to the infusion of grace, or spiritual being. Secondly, because as Adam was formed of the slime of the earth by supernatural power and order[[Gen 2:7||]], so Christ was born of the Virgin by the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost[[Luke 1:35||]]. Again, as from the side of Adam asleep a rib was taken, from which Eve was formed[[Gen 2:21||]], so from the side of Christ dying flowed the sacraments[[John 19:34||]], by which the Church is formed. But this reason comes back to the first.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit, quod Christus potentior erat ad salvandum, quam peccatum Adæ, seu Adam, ad perdendum. Sed non sicut delictum Adæ se habuit, ita et donum, id est, gratia Christi se habet, sed excellit. Sapientia namque vicit malitiam. Si enim in unius delicto, id est in originali Adæ peccato, multi mortui sunt, vitam gratiæ amittendo, et necessitatem moriendi incurrendo, hi scilicet in quos transfusum est originale peccatum; multo magis gratia Dei et donum Spiritus Sancti, in gratia, id est per singularem ac summam gratiam, virtutum perfectionem ac meritum, unius hominis Jesu Christi, qui est Deus et homo, in plures, id est in multos, abundavit, non in plures numero. Peccatum enim Adæ in omnes transiit (per hoc non oportet includi Virginem matrem), sed gratia Dei per Christum transiit in omnes electos. Erat autem in Christo gratia unionis, quæ non est quid creatum, sed Deus gratiose sive gratuite uniens sibi in unitate personali humanam naturam Christi. Estque in eo gratia capitis, per quam influit omnibus suis membris, seu cunctis fidelibus, quia de plenitudine ejus accepimus omnes: et ita gratia Dei nobis per gratiam Christi infunditur, et abundat in multis. Gratia tamen immediate a Deo creatur, sed Christus per suæ gratiæ plenitudinem est causa meritoria, et mediator per quem Deus gratiam nobis largitur.
paras.en: Next he shows that Christ was more powerful to save than the sin of Adam, or Adam, to destroy. [[5:15|But not as the offence|Sed non sicut delictum]], Adam's, stood, [[5:15|so also the gift|ita et donum]], that is, the grace of Christ stands, but it surpasses it. For wisdom has overcome malice[[Wis 7:30||]]. [[5:15|For if by the offence of one|Si enim in unius delicto]], that is, by the original sin of Adam, [[5:15|many died|multi mortui sunt]], losing the life of grace and incurring the necessity of dying, namely those into whom original sin was passed on; [[5:15|much more the grace of God and the gift|multo magis gratia Dei et donum]], the gift of the Holy Ghost, [[5:15|by the grace|in gratia]], that is, through the singular and highest grace, the perfection of virtues and the merit, [[5:15|of one man, Jesus Christ|unius hominis Jesu Christi]], who is God and man, [[5:15|hath abounded unto many|in plures abundavit]], that is, unto many, not unto more in number. For the sin of Adam passed into all (in which the Virgin Mother need not be included), but the grace of God through Christ passed into all the elect. Now there was in Christ the grace of union, which is not something created, but God graciously, or freely, uniting to himself in the unity of person the human nature of Christ. And there is in him the grace of the head, by which he flows into all his members, or all the faithful, since [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|de plenitudine ejus accepimus omnes]]: and so the grace of God is poured into us through the grace of Christ, and abounds in many. Yet grace is created immediately by God, but Christ, by the fulness of his grace, is the meritorious cause, and the mediator through whom God bestows grace on us.

paras.t: Et non sicut per unum peccatum, ita et donum: id est, non sic factum est per donum gratiæ Christi, quemadmodum factum est per unum originale peccatum Adæ; sed dispar est effectus peccati Adæ, et gratiæ Christi. Nam judicium quidem, id est sententia Dei, processit ex uno peccato originali Adæ, in condemnationem eorum in quos illud peccatum transfunditur, scilicet, ut divina visione priventur propter illud peccatum, nisi eis aliter succurratur. Gratia autem Christi procedit ex multis delictis in justificationem, id est, non solum unum ac originale, sed omnia etiam actualia peccata delendo, justificat, formaliter ponens animam in esse spirituali ac meritorio, ita ut impleatur universis virtutibus et donis Spiritus Sancti. Peccatum ergo Adæ non inficit alios, nisi uno peccato directe et immediate, videlicet originali; donum vero gratiæ Christi, omnia aufert peccata, et plurima tribuit bona.
paras.en: [[5:16|And not as it was by one sin, so also is the gift|Et non sicut per unum peccatum, ita et donum]]: that is, it has not been done through the gift of Christ's grace as it was done through the one original sin of Adam; but the effect of Adam's sin and of Christ's grace is unlike. [[5:16|For judgment indeed|Nam judicium quidem]], that is, God's sentence, went forth [[5:16|by one|ex uno]], from the one original sin of Adam, [[5:16|unto condemnation|in condemnationem]] of those into whom that sin is passed on, namely that they be deprived of the divine vision on account of that sin, unless they are helped otherwise. [[5:16|But grace|Gratia autem]], Christ's, proceeds [[5:16|of many offences unto justification|ex multis delictis in justificationem]], that is, it justifies by blotting out not only the one original sin but all actual sins too, formally setting the soul in spiritual and meritorious being, so that it is filled with all the virtues and gifts of the Holy Ghost. The sin of Adam, then, does not infect others save with one sin, directly and immediately, namely original sin; but the gift of Christ's grace takes away all sins and bestows very many goods.

paras.t: Si enim in unius delicto, id est si propter originale primi parentis peccatum, mors corporalis regnavit in omnibus peccato originali infectis, per unum, videlicet Adam, a quo culpa ista contrahitur; multo magis abundantiam gratiæ et donationis, id est remissionis peccatorum, vel, Donationis, id est virtutum quæ simul cum habitu gratiæ infunduntur, et justitiæ, id est operationis bonæ, […] Accipientes fideles a Deo, a quo est omne donum optimum et omne datum perfectum, in vita æterna, id est beatitudine consummata, regnabunt per unum Jesum Christum, per quem ad cœleste regnum perducuntur. Omnes autem Beati regnant in patria perfectissime super se ipsos, servientes Deo sine rebellione, cui servire, regnare est. Omnia quoque inferiora et dæmones subjecti sunt eis. Unde fatentur, loquentes ad Christum: Fecisti nos Deo nostro regnum et sacerdotes, et regnabimus super terram. Et alibi legitur: Judicabunt nationes et dominabuntur populis.
paras.en: [[5:17|For if by one man's offence|Si enim in unius delicto]], that is, if on account of the original sin of the first parent, [[5:17|death reigned|mors corporalis regnavit]], bodily death, in all who are infected with original sin, [[5:17|through one|per unum]], namely Adam, from whom this guilt is contracted; [[5:17|much more they who receive abundance of grace and of the gift|multo magis abundantiam gratiæ et donationis]], that is, of the remission of sins, or, *of the gift*, that is, of the virtues which are infused together with the habit of grace, [[5:17|and of justice|et justitiæ]], that is, of good working, […] [a line or two is missing from the transcription here] the faithful *receiving* it from God, from whom is [[Jas 1:17|Every best gift and every perfect gift|omne donum optimum et omne datum perfectum]], [[5:17|shall reign in life|in vita regnabunt]], eternal life, that is, consummated beatitude, [[5:17|through one, Jesus Christ|per unum Jesum Christum]], through whom they are led to the heavenly kingdom. And all the Blessed reign most perfectly in the fatherland over themselves, serving God without rebellion, whom to serve is to reign. All lower things and the demons too are subject to them. Hence they confess, speaking to Christ: [[Apoc 5:10|And hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests, and we shall reign on the earth|Fecisti nos Deo nostro regnum et sacerdotes, et regnabimus super terram]]. And elsewhere we read: [[Wis 3:8|They shall judge nations, and rule over people|Judicabunt nationes et dominabuntur populis]].

paras.t: Igitur, sicut per unius, scilicet Adæ, delictum originale, quod etiam erat actuale et personale quantum ad ipsum Adam, processit sententia Dei in omnes homines hoc peccato infectos, in condemnationem eorum, ut dictum est; sic et per unius, videlicet Christi, justitiam, id est justam sanctificationem atque sanctissimam conversationem, prodiit sententia Dei in omnes homines in justificationem vitæ ipsorum, id est in remissionem peccatorum et infusionem virtutum: quia per meritum Christi omnes justificati atque salvati sunt, quantum est ex parte Salvatoris. Aliqui tamen obicem ponunt saluti et gratiæ; aliqui quoque privantur applicatione virtutis et meriti gratiæ, propter quod a beatitudinis adeptione impediuntur, ut pueri non baptizati. Eo itaque modo omnes per Christum justificantur, sicut omnes in eo benedicuntur.
paras.en: [[5:18|Therefore, as by the offence of one|Igitur, sicut per unius, scilicet Adæ, delictum]], namely Adam's original offence, which was also actual and personal as regards Adam himself, God's sentence went forth [[5:18|unto all men|in omnes homines]] infected with this sin, [[5:18|to condemnation|in condemnationem]] of them, as has been said; [[5:18|so also by the justice of one|sic et per unius, videlicet Christi, justitiam]], namely Christ's, that is, his just holiness and most holy way of life, God's sentence went forth [[5:18|unto all men to justification of life|in omnes homines in justificationem vitæ]], their life, that is, to the remission of sins and the infusion of virtues: for through the merit of Christ all have been justified and saved, as far as lies on the Saviour's side. Yet some put an obstacle in the way of salvation and grace; and some are deprived of the application of the power and merit of grace, on account of which they are hindered from attaining beatitude, as unbaptized children. In this way, then, all are justified through Christ, as all are blessed in him.

paras.t: Sicut enim per inobedientiam unius hominis, id est per transgressionem primi parentis, peccatores constituti sunt multi, originale ab ipso trahendo, vel ejus inobedientiam assequendo; ita et per unius, scilicet Christi, […] qui factus est pro nobis obediens usque ad mortem; qui loquitur: Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio; justi constituentur […] per ipsum, veniam per pœnitentiam et gratiam, imitandoque ejus justitiam. Christus enim passus est pro nobis, nobis […] relinquens exemplum, ut sequamur vestigia ejus.
paras.en: [[5:19|For as by the disobedience of one man|Sicut enim per inobedientiam unius hominis]], that is, by the transgression of the first parent, [[5:19|many were made sinners|peccatores constituti sunt multi]], by contracting original sin from him, or by following his disobedience; [[5:19|so also by the|ita et per unius]] […] [the word *obedience* and some lines are missing from the transcription] of one, namely Christ, who was made for us [[Phil 2:8|obedient unto death|obediens usque ad mortem]]; who says: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]; [[5:19|many shall be made just|justi constituentur]] […] through him, pardon through penance and grace, and by imitating his justice. For [[1 Pet 2:21|Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example that you should follow his steps|Christus enim passus est pro nobis, nobis relinquens exemplum, ut sequamur vestigia ejus]] [Denis: "leaving us an example, that we should follow"].

paras.t: Declarata abundantia et sufficientia gratiæ Christi, ostendit Apostolus insufficientiam legis, ut tota spes hominum constituatur in Christo, atque ad ejus pietatem omnes confugiant. Lex autem scripta data per Moysen, subintravit post legem naturalem, naturalisque rationis obtenebrationem, ut abundaret delictum. Hæc dictio, Ut, tenetur hoc loco consecutive, non causaliter. Ex legis quippe latione consecuta est multiplicatio iniquitatis et aggravatio ejus: Primo, quoniam quanto post legem peccatum magis cognoscebatur, tanto gravius erat peccatum. Secundo, quia post legem erant multa illicita, quæ ante licita erant. Tertio, quia lex peccata prohibendo, ostendit peccata: sicque concupiscentia provocabatur, quia Nitimur in vetitum semper, cupimusque negata. Quarto, quoniam non præstabat auxilium gratiæ, qua vitantur peccata. Hanc autem insufficientiam voluit Deus esse in lege, ut omnes ad Christum confugerent, ejus cupiendo adventum, nec in propriis viribus habendo fiduciam.
paras.en: Having made plain the abundance and sufficiency of Christ's grace, the Apostle shows the insufficiency of the law, so that the whole hope of men may be set in Christ and all may flee to his mercy. [[5:20|Now the law entered in|Lex autem subintravit]], the written law, given through Moses, entered in after the natural law and the darkening of natural reason, [[5:20|that sin might abound|ut abundaret delictum]]. The word *that* is taken here consecutively, not causally. For from the giving of the law there followed a multiplying of iniquity and an aggravating of it. First, because the better sin was known after the law, the graver the sin was. Secondly, because after the law many things were unlawful which before were lawful. Thirdly, because the law, by forbidding sins, showed sins: and so concupiscence was provoked, since *We ever strive for what is forbidden, and desire what is denied* [a line of Ovid, *Amores* III, iv, 17]. Fourthly, because it did not give the help of grace by which sins are avoided. God willed this insufficiency to be in the law so that all might flee to Christ, longing for his coming, and not trusting in their own strength.

paras.t: Ubi autem abundavit delictum, videlicet in Judæis sub lege constitutis, quibus data est lex ut abundaret delictum in eis, superabundavit et gratia Christi, qui factus est sub lege, natus ex populo Judæorum. Propter quod ait: Salus ex Judæis est; et alibi, Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel. Denique Apostoli, qui primitias Spiritus Sancti receperunt, et primitiva Ecclesia, cui maximam gratiam contulit Christus, ex populo fuerant Judæorum. Ad hoc autem et eo tenore superabundavit gratia ubi abundavit delictum, ut sicut regnavit peccatum in mortem, id est, suo infelici dominio atque demerito perduxit, imo et introduxit, in mortem damnationis æternæ, privationemque gratiæ, quæ est mors animæ in præsenti: peccatum enim gratiam aufert, et pœnam inducit; ita et gratia Dei regnet in nobis per justitiam, id est justitiæ exercitationem, ita ut habitus gratiæ tendat in actum, sicque perducat in vitam æternam, quæ est merces et consummatio, per Jesum Christum Dominum nostrum, sine cujus auxilio nil boni valemus. Insuper videmus in multis impleri quod hic ait Apostolus. Frequenter enim qui gravius peccaverunt, post conversionem suam ferventiores sunt ceteris: et ita in quorum cordibus abundavit malitia, abundat et gratia. Malum namque occasionaliter causa est boni, in quantum recordatio præteritæ iniquitatis facit hominem se ipsum magis despicere, damnationem æternam amplius formidare, misericordiam Dei plenius admirari ardentiusque diligere. Unde Salvator in Evangelio protestatur: Cui plus dimittitur, plus diligit. Istud tamen non semper contingit, quia et absolute loquendo, et ceteris paribus, innocens plus tenetur Deum amare, plusque amatur a Deo, quam peccator conversus, secundum Thomam.
paras.en: [[5:20|And where sin abounded|Ubi autem abundavit delictum]], namely in the Jews placed under the law, to whom the law was given that sin might abound in them, [[5:20|grace did more abound|superabundavit et gratia]], the grace of Christ, who was [[Gal 4:4|made under the law|factus est sub lege]], born of the people of the Jews. For which reason he says: [[John 4:22|salvation is of the Jews|Salus ex Judæis est]]; and elsewhere: [[Matt 15:24|I was not sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]]. Lastly, the Apostles, who received [[Rom 8:23|the firstfruits of the Spirit|primitias Spiritus]], and the early Church, on which Christ bestowed the greatest grace, were of the people of the Jews. And grace more abounded where sin abounded to this end and in this tenor, [[5:21|That as sin hath reigned to death|ut sicut regnavit peccatum in mortem]], that is, by its unhappy dominion and demerit has led, nay brought, into the death of eternal damnation, and the privation of grace, which is the death of the soul in the present life: for sin takes away grace and brings in punishment; [[5:21|so also grace might reign by justice|ita et gratia regnet per justitiam]], the grace of God reign in us, through justice, that is, the exercise of justice, so that the habit of grace tends to act, and so leads [[5:21|unto life everlasting|in vitam æternam]], which is the reward and the consummation, [[5:21|through Jesus Christ our Lord|per Jesum Christum Dominum nostrum]], without whose help we can do no good[[John 15:5||]]. Moreover, we see what the Apostle says here fulfilled in many. For often those who have sinned more gravely are more fervent than the rest after their conversion: and so in those in whose hearts malice abounded, grace abounds too. For evil is occasionally the cause of good, inasmuch as the remembrance of past iniquity makes a man despise himself more, fear eternal damnation more, wonder more fully at the mercy of God and love it more ardently. Hence the Saviour declares in the Gospel: he to whom more is forgiven loves more[[Luke 7:47||]]. Yet this does not always happen, since, speaking absolutely and other things being equal, the innocent man is more bound to love God, and is more loved by God, than the converted sinner, according to Thomas.

6.title: Expositio capituli sexti: Quid ergo dicemus?
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: What shall we say, then?

paras.t: Removet sanctus Apostolus in hujus capituli exordio quemdam errorem, qui ex prædictis sumpsit originem. Quidam enim perversi audientes dixisse Apostolum. Ubi abundavit delictum superabundat et gratia, asseruerunt, atque Apostolum id docuisse dixerunt, quod permanendum esset in vitiis, et abundanter peccandum, ut postmodum gratia superabundet. Hoc reprobans ait : Quid ergo dicemus? id est, si juxta prædicta, superabundat gratia ubi abundavit malitia, an hoc dicendum est quod sequitur, scilicet, Manebimus in peccato, id est, an perseverandum est nobis ad tempus in vitiis, ut quidam nos dicere arbitrantur, ut gratia abundet in nobis postea? Absit, id est, ita dicendum non est. Cujus ratio subinfertur. Qui enim mortui sumus ipsi peccato, id est, vitiis mortificati, et a peccato liberati per pretium sanguinis Christi, per gratiam Baptismi, per Pœnitentiæ sacramentum. Mortuum esse peccato, est a peccato esse ereptum, vel secundum virtutum habitus operari. Quomodo adhuc, id est iterum, vivemus in illo, id est, operabimur opera tenebrarum et consentiemus suggestioni peccati? tanquam dicat : Nec decet, nec licet, nec expedit nos taliter recidivare. Nam sicut in naturalibus non est reditus a morte in vitam, sic in moralibus non est naturaliter regressus a morte culpæ ad vitam gratiæ. Utrumque tamen interdum contingit per omnipotentiam atque clementiam Creatoris.
paras.en: At the beginning of this chapter the holy Apostle removes an error which took its origin from what has been said. For certain perverse men, hearing that the Apostle had said, [[Rom 5:20|where sin abounded, grace did more abound|Ubi abundavit delictum superabundat et gratia]], asserted, and said that the Apostle had taught it, that one should remain in vices and sin abundantly, so that afterwards grace might abound the more. Rejecting this he says: [[6:1|What shall we say, then?|Quid ergo dicemus?]] That is, if, according to what has been said, grace more abounds where malice abounded, is what follows to be said, namely, [[6:1|Shall we continue in sin|Manebimus in peccato]], that is, must we persevere for a time in vices, as some think we say, [[6:1|that grace may abound?|ut gratia abundet]] in us afterwards? [[6:2|God forbid!|Absit]], that is, it is not to be said so. The reason for this is added. [[6:2|For we that are dead to sin|Qui enim mortui sumus ipsi peccato]], that is, mortified to vices, and freed from sin by the price of Christ's blood, by the grace of Baptism, by the sacrament of Penance. To be dead to sin is to be rescued from sin, or to act according to the habits of the virtues. [[6:2|how shall we live any longer therein?|quomodo adhuc vivemus in illo?]], *any longer*, that is, again, that is, do the works of darkness and consent to the suggestion of sin? As if he were saying: it is neither fitting, nor lawful, nor expedient for us to fall back in this way. For as in natural things there is no return from death to life, so in moral things there is by nature no going back from the death of fault to the life of grace. Yet both sometimes happen through the omnipotence and clemency of the Creator.

paras.t: Deinde docet Apostolus quomodo mortui sumus ipsi peccato. […] […]tiis loti in sacro Baptismatis fonte, in Christo Jesu, id est in institutione, fide et operatione Christi (Christus enim Baptismum instituit, dicens, Docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti ; ipse quoque fidem Trinitatis edocuit, principaliterque baptizat, secundum quod Deus : sic enim purgat a culpa ; sacerdos vero minister est ejus), in morte ipsius, id est merito mortis ejus, seu per virtutem suæ passionis, a qua Baptismus efficientiam habet, baptizati sumus? Vel, In morte ejus, id est in similitudine mortis Christi baptizati sumus, quatenus, sicut Christus semel mortuus est carne, et semper vivit spiritu, sic nos per Baptismum semel mortui iniquitati, deinceps semper vivamus justitiæ. Trina namque immersio signat triduum sepulturæ seu mortis ; elevatio autem, resurrectionem ejus post triduum. Huic secundæ expositioni consonat littera sequens. Ostendens enim quomodo in morte Christi baptizati dicamur, adjecit :
paras.en: Next the Apostle teaches how we are dead to sin. […] [the beginning of v. 3 is lost in the transcription] [washed from our vi]ces in the sacred font of Baptism, [[6:3|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, in the institution, faith and working of Christ (for Christ instituted Baptism, saying, [[Matt 28:19|teach ye all nations: baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost|Docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti]]; he also taught the faith of the Trinity, and baptizes principally, as he is God: for so he cleanses from fault; but the priest is his minister), [[6:3|in his death|in morte ipsius]], that is, by the merit of his death, or by the power of his passion, from which Baptism has its efficacy, [[6:3|are baptized|baptizati sumus]]? Or, *in his death*, that is, we are baptized in the likeness of Christ's death, so that as Christ died once in the flesh and lives for ever in the spirit[[1 Pet 3:18||]], so we, dead once to iniquity through Baptism, may live henceforth for ever to justice. For the threefold immersion signifies the three days of burial or death; and the lifting out, his resurrection after three days. With this second exposition the following text agrees. For, showing how we are said to be baptized in Christ's death, he added:

paras.t: Consepulti enim sumus cum illo, id est, Christo sepulto assimilati sumus, vel per fidem cum eo sepulti : et hoc, per Baptismum, id est in ipso Baptismo : mersio enim baptizandi in aqua, designat sepulturam Christi sub terra ; in mortem peccati, id est ad peccati destructionem, videlicet ut moriamur peccato. Ut quomodo surrexit Christus a mortuis, id est a loco atque consortio cadaverum mortuorum : ipse enim solus fuit inter mortuos liber, cujus caro non vidit corruptionem ; per gloriam, id est majestatem sed divina virtute surrexit. Potest quoque per gloriam Patris intelligi Verbum Dei, quod humanam naturam assumpsit, et Christum hominem, imo se ipsum secundum quod homo est, suscitavit. Scriptum est enim : Gloria patris, filius sapiens. De hac gloria Patris seu Filio Dei scriptum est : Revelabitur gloria Domini, et videbit omnis caro Salutare Dei nostri. Ita et nos in novitate vitæ ambulemus, id est, pristinis vitiis exstirpatis, spiritualiter reformemur et christiformiter conversemur, quatenus renovetur ut aquilæ juventus nostra, refloreatque et reviviscat, vegetetur, crescat ac perficiatur quotidie spiritus noster in splendore gratiæ Dei.
paras.en: [[6:4|For we are buried together with him|Consepulti enim sumus cum illo]], that is, we have been made like to Christ buried, or buried with him by faith: and this [[6:4|by baptism|per Baptismum]], that is, in Baptism itself: for the immersion of the one baptized in the water signifies the burial of Christ beneath the earth; [[6:4|into death|in mortem]] of sin, that is, for the destruction of sin, namely that we may die to sin. [[6:4|that, as Christ is risen from the dead|Ut quomodo surrexit Christus a mortuis]], that is, from the place and company of the bodies of the dead: for he alone was [[Ps 87:6|Free among the dead|inter mortuos liber]], whose flesh did not see corruption[[Ps 15:10||]]; *by the glory*, that is, the majesty [… a line is lost here in the transcription …] but rose by divine power. By [[6:4|the glory of the Father|gloriam Patris]] may also be understood the Word of God, who assumed human nature, and raised up Christ the man, indeed himself as he is man. For it is written: The glory of the father is a wise son[[Prov 10:1||]]. Of this glory of the Father, or Son of God, it is written: [[Is 40:5|And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see|Revelabitur gloria Domini, et videbit omnis caro]] the salvation of our God [Denis's ending is that of Luke 3:6]. [[6:4|so we also may walk in newness of life|Ita et nos in novitate vitæ ambulemus]], that is, our former vices rooted out, let us be spiritually reformed and live in Christ's form, so that [[Ps 102:5|thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle's|renovetur ut aquilæ juventus nostra]] [Denis has "our youth"], and our spirit may flourish again and revive, be quickened, grow and be perfected daily in the splendour of the grace of God.

paras.t: Si enim complantati facti sumus similitudini mortis ejus, id est, si more plantæ seu arboris, eradicati fuerimus a similitudine præcedentium vitiorum, et facti fuerimus complantati, id est firmiter inhærentes et conformati similitudini mortis ejus, id est vestigiis dominicæ passionis, conformando nos passionibus Christi, moriendoque culpæ, sicut ipse mortuus est pœnis peccati; simul et resurrectionis erimus, id est, tunc etiam complantabimur similitudini resurrectionis Christi, ambulando in novitate vitæ, quæ per Christi resurrectionem figuratur. Mors nempe et resurrectio Christi non solum sunt res, sed etiam sacramenta seu signa. Mors ergo Christi significat veteris ac vitiosæ conversationis occisionem; resurrectio vero, spiritualem mentis renovationem. In Baptismo autem morimur pristinæ vitæ, id est actibus vitiorum. Si ergo in hac vitiorum mortificatione manserimus, non redeundo ad vitia, tunc resurrectioni Christi similes erimus, cœlestem conversationem habendo in terra, quemadmodum alibi dicit Apostolus : Si commortui sumus, et convivemus.
paras.en: [[6:5|For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death|Si enim complantati facti sumus similitudini mortis ejus]], that is, if, in the manner of a plant or tree, we have been rooted out of the likeness of our former vices, and have been made planted together, that is, firmly cleaving and conformed to the likeness of his death, that is, to the footsteps of the Lord's passion, conforming ourselves to the sufferings of Christ and dying to fault, as he died to the punishments of sin; [[6:5|we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection|simul et resurrectionis erimus]], that is, then we shall also be planted together in the likeness of Christ's resurrection, walking in newness of life, which is figured by Christ's resurrection. For the death and resurrection of Christ are not only things but also sacraments, or signs. Christ's death therefore signifies the slaying of the old and vicious way of life; his resurrection, the spiritual renewal of the mind. And in Baptism we die to our former life, that is, to the acts of vices. If then we remain in this mortifying of vices, not returning to vices, we shall then be like to Christ's resurrection, having a heavenly way of life on earth, as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Tim 2:11|if we be dead with him, we shall live also with him|Si commortui sumus, et convivemus]].

paras.t: Hoc scientes quia vetus homo noster, id est quilibet nostrum secundum vitiosam ac veterem conversationem, simul crucifixus est, id est, simul cum Christo affixus est cruci per præfigurationem et obligationem. Per hoc enim quod crucifixus est Christus, præmonstratum est quod quilibet nostrum, si velit salvari, debeat Christum sequi, tollendo crucem suam quotidie. Ad hoc quoque obligat nos crucifixio Christi Domini nostri, quoniam non est servus major domino suo. Vel, Vetus homo noster, id est quilibet nostrum secundum originale peccatum a veteri Adam contractum, simul crucifixus est, id est huic peccato mortificatus, quia in Christi passione liberati sumus ab isto peccato, ita ut non imputetur nobis in culpam, nec propter ipsum obligemur ad pœnam damni, videlicet divinæ visionis carentiam. Ut destruatur corpus peccati, id est, quatenus caro nostra multis peccatis maculata destruatur, non quantum ad esse naturæ, sed quantum ad esse culpæ, quemadmodum alibi ait Apostolus : Mortificate membra vestra quæ sunt super terram; et Christus, Si oculus tuus scandalizat te, erue eum et projice abs te. Hinc etiam a Sapiente dicitur : Verte impios, et non erunt. Ut ultra non serviamus peccato, id est, non vincamur a malo, non succumbamus tentationi, nec ratio nostra subdatur iniquitati, sed eam sibi subjiciat. Unde scriptum est : Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati. Et Petrus : Iniqui sunt servi corruptionis : a quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est. — Alii quos legi, ita exponunt : Vetus homo noster, id est fomes peccati, simul crucifixus est, id est, Christi crucifixione et ejus passionis virtute debilitatus est. Vel, Vetus homo noster, id est conversatio vitiosa (de quo homine Ephesiis ait Apostolus : Exuite veterem hominem), simul crucifixus est, id est, morte Christi deleta est; ut destruatur corpus, id est universitas atque congeries, peccati. De quo corpore Salvator : Si oculus tuus, inquit, fuerit nequam, totum corpus tuum tenebrosum erit, id est operum tuorum congeries.
paras.en: [[6:6|Knowing this, that our old man|Hoc scientes quia vetus homo noster]], that is, each of us according to the vicious and old way of life, [[6:6|is crucified with him|simul crucifixus est]], that is, together with Christ has been fixed to the cross by prefiguring and by obligation. For by Christ's being crucified it was shown beforehand that each of us, if he wishes to be saved, must follow Christ, taking up his cross daily[[Luke 9:23||]]. To this the crucifixion of Christ our Lord also binds us, since [[John 13:16|The servant is not greater than his lord|non est servus major domino suo]]. Or, *our old man*, that is, each of us according to the original sin contracted from the old Adam, *is crucified with him*, that is, mortified to this sin, since in Christ's passion we were freed from this sin, so that it is not imputed to us as fault, nor are we bound for it to the punishment of loss, namely the lack of the divine vision. [[6:6|that the body of sin may be destroyed|Ut destruatur corpus peccati]], that is, so that our flesh, stained with many sins, may be destroyed, not as to the being of nature but as to the being of fault, as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[Col 3:5|Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth|Mortificate membra vestra quæ sunt super terram]]; and Christ, [[Matt 18:9|if thy eye scandalize thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee|Si oculus tuus scandalizat te, erue eum et projice abs te]]. Hence too it is said by the Wise Man: [[Prov 12:7|Turn the wicked, and they shall not be|Verte impios, et non erunt]]. [[6:6|to the end that we may serve sin no longer|Ut ultra non serviamus peccato]], that is, that we may not be overcome by evil, nor give way to temptation, nor our reason be made subject to iniquity, but subject it to itself. Hence it is written: [[John 8:34|whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin|Omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati]]. And Peter: [[2 Pet 2:19|they themselves are the slaves of corruption|Iniqui sunt servi corruptionis]]: [[2 Pet 2:19|For by whom a man is overcome, of the same also he is the slave|a quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est]]. Others whom I have read expound it thus: *our old man*, that is, the tinder of sin, *is crucified with him*, that is, weakened by Christ's crucifixion and the power of his passion. Or, *our old man*, that is, the vicious way of life (of which man the Apostle says to the Ephesians, Put off the old man[[Eph 4:22||]]), *is crucified with him*, that is, blotted out by Christ's death; *that the body of sin may be destroyed*, that is, the whole sum and heap of sin. Of which body the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:23|if thy eye be evil thy whole body shall be darksome|Si oculus tuus, inquit, fuerit nequam, totum corpus tuum tenebrosum erit]] (he says), that is, the heap of your works.

paras.t: Qui enim mortuus est peccato, id est a peccato liberatus ; vel, Qui mortuus est, id est configuratus morti Christi, per susceptionem Baptismatis; justificatus est a peccato, id est, liber factus ab eo, nec subjacet vitio. Baptismus enim aufert pœnam et culpam.
paras.en: [[6:7|For he that is dead|Qui enim mortuus est]] to sin, that is, freed from sin; or, *he that is dead*, that is, conformed to the death of Christ by receiving Baptism; [[6:7|is justified from sin|justificatus est a peccato]], that is, made free from it, and is not subject to vice. For Baptism takes away punishment and fault.

paras.t: Si autem mortui sumus cum Christo, id est passionibus ejus conformati, et ita mortui culpæ, quomodo Christus mortuus est pœnæ, videlicet sine recidivo; credimus quia simul etiam vivemus cum illo, non solum vita gratiæ in præsenti, sed etiam vita gloriæ in futuro. Scientes per fidem certissimam : de qua scientia ait Job, Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit; quod Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur, id est, de cetero non morietur : sicut Origenes fertur dixisse, quod Christus secundo pro dæmonibus passurus est. Surrexit enim non solum ad immortalem, sed etiam ad impassibilem vitam. Mors corporalis illi ultra non dominabitur, prævalendo vitæ ejus corporali, seu animam separando a corpore : et multo minus mors gehennæ dominata est Christo. Quod enim mortuus est peccato, id est nostrorum peccatorum demerito, et propter expiationem vitiorum nostrorum, juxta illud Threnorum, Christus Dominus captus est in peccatis nostris; et illud Isaiæ, Attritus est propter scelera nostra; mortuus est semel, in die Parasceves. De qua die Dominus per Prophetam loquitur : Auferam iniquitatem terræ illius in die una. Tunc enim Deus abstulit peccata Ecclesiæ, quæ est terra Christi, per meritum passionis ipsius. Quod autem vivit post resurrectionem, vivit Deo, id est ad gloriam Dei.
paras.en: [[6:8|Now, if we be dead with Christ|Si autem mortui sumus cum Christo]], that is, conformed to his sufferings, and so dead to fault as Christ died to punishment, namely without relapse, [[6:8|we believe that we shall live also together with Christ|credimus quia simul etiam vivemus cum illo]], not only with the life of grace in the present but also with the life of glory in the future. [[6:9|Knowing|Scientes]] by most certain faith (of which knowledge Job says, [[Job 19:25|For I know that my Redeemer liveth|Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit]]), [[6:9|that Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more|quod Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur]], that is, will not die again: as Origen is said to have said that Christ is to suffer a second time for the demons. For he rose not only to an immortal but also to an impassible life. [[6:9|Death shall no more have dominion over him|Mors corporalis illi ultra non dominabitur]], bodily death, prevailing over his bodily life, or separating the soul from the body: and much less has the death of hell had dominion over Christ. [[6:10|For in that he died to sin|Quod enim mortuus est peccato]], that is, through the demerit of our sins, and to expiate our vices, according to that of Lamentations, [[Lam 4:20|Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins|Christus Dominus captus est in peccatis nostris]]; and that of Isaias, [[Is 53:5|he was bruised for our sins|Attritus est propter scelera nostra]]; [[6:10|he died once|mortuus est semel]], on the day of the Parasceve. Of which day the Lord speaks through the Prophet: [[Zach 3:9|I will take away the iniquity of that land in one day|Auferam iniquitatem terræ illius in die una]]. For then God took away the sins of the Church, which is Christ's land, by the merit of his passion. [[6:10|but in that he liveth|Quod autem vivit]] after the resurrection, [[6:10|he liveth unto God|vivit Deo]], that is, to the glory of God.

paras.t: Ita et vos, o Romani, imo quicumque fideles, existimate vos ipsos mortuos quidem esse peccato, id est liberatos a vitiis merito Salvatoris, viventes autem Deo, id est deiformiter atque deificè, scilicet ad gloriam Dei, operando divina, contemplando atque amando cælestia. Vivere equidem Deo, aliud nihil est nisi operari ea quæ Deo sunt placita, et divinæ vitæ utcumque assimilari. In Christo Jesu Domino nostro, id est per gratiam Christi, et permanendo in ipso, tanquam in mediatore, salvatore et capite. Ipse enim profitetur : Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et arescet.
paras.en: [[6:11|So do you also|Ita et vos]], O Romans, indeed all the faithful, [[6:11|reckon that you are dead to sin|existimate vos ipsos mortuos quidem esse peccato]], that is, freed from vices by the merit of the Saviour, [[6:11|but alive unto God|viventes autem Deo]], that is, in a godlike and deifying way, namely to the glory of God, doing divine works, contemplating and loving heavenly things. For to live to God is nothing else than to do the things that are pleasing to God, and to be made in some way like the divine life. [[6:11|in Christ Jesus our Lord|In Christo Jesu Domino nostro]], that is, through the grace of Christ, and by abiding in him, as in our mediator, saviour and head. For he himself declares: [[John 15:6|If any one abide not in me, he shall be cast forth as a branch and shall wither|Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et arescet]].

paras.t: Non ergo regnet, id est, virtutibus non prævaleat, nec rationem subjiciat, peccatum actuale, vel fomes peccati : qui dicitur peccatum causaliter, quia inclinat ad culpam, et quamvis transeat reatu, permanet tamen actu, in quantum est pœna, et virtuosæ exercitationis spiritualisque pugnæ materia; in vestro mortali corpore proclivo ad vitia : de quo scriptum est: Corpus quod corrumpitur, aggravat animam; ut obediatis concupiscentiis ejus, id est, carnalibus desideriis seu fomitis inclinationibus consentiatis. Hoc namque præposterum est et perversum, ut sensualitas rationi prævaleat, aut caro dominetur spiritui. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico legitur : Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere. Sed neque exhibeatis membra vestra arma iniquitatis peccato, id est, membris corporis vestri seu organis nolite abuti, extendendo ea ad mala; nec fiant arma iniquitatis, id est instrumenta culpæ, peccato, id est ad executionem peccati, quæ a Deo collata sunt, ut sint instrumenta virtutum, quatenus anima per corporis membra tendat in actum virtutum exteriorem. Sed exhibete vos Deo, id est, ad Dei obsequium vos aptate, et animas vestras Deo per sanctam obedientiam immolate, quatenus, sicut totum quod habetis et estis, a Deo recepistis, sic totum ei reddatis, serviendo ei mente et corpore, tanquam ex mortuis viventes, id est sicut a morte culpæ ad vitam gratiæ suscitati; et membra vestra exhibete arma justitiæ Deo, exercendo per ea actus virtutum et opera æquitatis, Deo, id est ad Dei honorem ac laudem. […]
paras.en: [[6:12|Let not sin therefore reign|Non ergo regnet]], that is, prevail over the virtues, nor make reason subject, actual sin, or the tinder of sin, which is called sin causally, because it inclines to fault, and though it passes as to guilt, yet remains in act, inasmuch as it is a punishment and the matter of virtuous exercise and spiritual combat; [[6:12|in your mortal body|in vestro mortali corpore]], prone to vices: of which it is written, [[Wis 9:15|the corruptible body is a load upon the soul|Corpus quod corrumpitur, aggravat animam]]; [[6:12|so as to obey the lusts thereof|ut obediatis concupiscentiis ejus]], that is, consent to carnal desires or the inclinations of the tinder. For this is preposterous and perverse, that sensuality should prevail over reason, or the flesh rule the spirit. For which reason we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 18:30|Go not after thy lusts, but turn away from thy own will|Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere]] [the margin reads Eccli. xxxvi, 30]. [[6:13|Neither yield ye your members as instruments of iniquity unto sin|Sed neque exhibeatis membra vestra arma iniquitatis peccato]], that is, do not misuse the members or organs of your body by stretching them out to evil; nor let them become *instruments* [*arma*, "weapons"] *of iniquity*, that is, tools of fault, *unto sin*, that is, for carrying out sin, which were given by God to be instruments of the virtues, so that the soul may tend through the members of the body to the outward act of the virtues. [[6:13|but present yourselves to God|Sed exhibete vos Deo]], that is, fit yourselves for the service of God, and offer up your souls to God by holy obedience, so that, as you have received from God all that you have and are[[1 Cor 4:7||]], so you may give it all back to him, serving him in mind and body, [[6:13|as those that are alive from the dead|tanquam ex mortuis viventes]], that is, as raised from the death of fault to the life of grace; [[6:13|and your members as instruments of justice unto God|et membra vestra exhibete arma justitiæ Deo]], doing through them acts of virtue and works of equity, *unto God*, that is, to the honour and praise of God. [… the beginning of v. 14 is lost in the transcription …]

paras.t: tur, necessitatem imponendo, dummodo ad Christi gratiam confugiatis. Vel, Peccatum, id est fomes peccati, vobis non dominabitur, trahendo vos ad peccatum mortale. Repressa namque et diminuta est inclinatio fomitis per gratiam Christi, ita ut stantes in gratia gratum faciente, possint omne peccatum mortale vitare : quod non possunt adulti qui gratia carent, sicut nec gratiam habentes vitare possunt omnia venialia, saltem diu. Sicut enim in istis sensualitas non est rationi perfecte subjecta, propter quod interdum venialiter peccant ; ita in illis non est ratio Deo subjecta cum debito ordine ultimi finis, idcirco diu vivere nequeunt sine mortali. Non enim estis sub lege Mosaica, quæ bona præcepit, et mala prohibuit, gratiam vero adimplendi non præstitit, sed sub gratia evangelicæ legis et Christi : ideo peccatum vobis non dominabitur, si feceritis quod in vobis est.
paras.en: […] by imposing necessity, provided you take refuge in the grace of Christ. Or, [[6:14|sin|Peccatum]], that is, the tinder of sin, [[6:14|shall not have dominion over you|vobis non dominabitur]], drawing you to mortal sin. For the inclination of the tinder has been checked and diminished by the grace of Christ, so that those who stand in sanctifying grace can avoid every mortal sin: which adults without grace cannot do, just as those who have grace cannot avoid all venial sins, at least for long. For as in these sensuality is not perfectly subject to reason, which is why they sometimes sin venially, so in those reason is not subject to God with the due order of the last end, and therefore they cannot live long without mortal sin. [[6:14|for you are not under the law|Non enim estis sub lege]] of Moses, which commanded good things and forbade evil but did not give the grace to fulfil them, [[6:14|but under grace|sed sub gratia]] of the law of the Gospel and of Christ: therefore sin will not have dominion over you, if you do what is in you.

paras.t: Circa hoc movet Apostolus quod vidit moveri posse ab aliis. Quid ergo restat ? Peccabimus, quoniam non sumus sub lege veteri, sed sub gratia ? id est, an hoc licet ut gratia Dei abutamur, ideo peccando securius, quia a minis et pœnis temporalibus legis liberati sumus ? Absit. Hoc enim vile atque perversum esset, sicut ostendunt sequentia. An nescitis quoniam cui exhibuistis vos servos ad obediendum, id est, cui vos sponte subjecistis, servi estis ejus cui obedistis ? Hoc palam est. Ad rationem enim servi pertinet obtemperare mandato alterius. Sive peccati ad mortem, id est, si exhibuistis vos servos peccato, servi estis peccati ad mortem culpæ in via, et ad mortem pœnæ in gehenna : ad hæc enim perducit servitus culpæ ; sive obeditionis ad justitiam, id est, si exhibuistis vos servos obedientiæ divinorum mandatorum, facti estis servi obedientiæ hujus ad justitiam, id est ad hoc ut justi sitis.
paras.en: Here the Apostle raises what he saw could be raised by others. [[6:15|What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace?|Quid ergo restat ? Peccabimus, quoniam non sumus sub lege veteri, sed sub gratia]] That is, is it lawful to abuse the grace of God, sinning the more securely because we have been freed from the threats and temporal punishments of the law? [[6:15|God forbid!|Absit]] For this would be vile and perverse, as what follows shows. [[6:16|Know you not that to whom you yield yourselves servants to obey|An nescitis quoniam cui exhibuistis vos servos ad obediendum]], that is, to whom you have freely subjected yourselves, [[6:16|his servants you are whom you obey|servi estis ejus cui obedistis]]? This is plain: for it belongs to the notion of a servant to obey another's command. [[6:16|whether it be of sin unto death|Sive peccati ad mortem]], that is, if you have yielded yourselves servants to sin, you are servants of sin unto the death of fault on the way, and the death of punishment in hell: for to these the service of fault leads; [[6:16|or of obedience unto justice|sive obeditionis ad justitiam]], that is, if you have yielded yourselves servants to obedience to the divine commandments, you have become servants of this obedience unto justice, that is, to the end that you may be just.

paras.t: Gratias autem refero Deo, cui de omni bono agenda est gratiarum actio, quod fuistis ante vestram conversionem servi peccati; obedistis autem ex corde, id est animo prompto atque spontaneo, in eam formam doctrinæ, id est in institutionem ac seriem evangelicæ disciplinæ, operando secundum præcepta et consilia Christi, in qua doctrina seu forma traditi estis scholæ Christi sive Ecclesiæ, ut tenendo hanc formam, sitis filii ac discipuli Christi et Ecclesiæ. Liberati autem a peccato, non solum per Christi passionem, sed etiam per diligentem vitiorum evitationem : quæ tamen evitatio vobis per gratiam Christi confertur; servi facti estis justitiæ, id est, justitiæ subjecti estis, implendo præcepta justitiæ.
paras.en: [[6:17|But thanks be to God|Gratias autem refero Deo]], to whom thanks must be given for every good, [[6:17|that you were the servants of sin|quod fuistis servi peccati]] before your conversion; [[6:17|but have obeyed from the heart|obedistis autem ex corde]], that is, with a ready and willing mind, [[6:17|unto that form of doctrine|in eam formam doctrinæ]], that is, unto the institution and order of the discipline of the Gospel, acting according to the precepts and counsels of Christ, [[6:17|into which you have been delivered|in qua doctrina seu forma traditi estis]], the doctrine or form, to the school of Christ or of the Church, so that by holding this form you may be sons and disciples of Christ and of the Church. [[6:18|Being then freed from sin|Liberati autem a peccato]], not only by Christ's passion but also by careful avoiding of vices (which avoiding, however, is given you by the grace of Christ), [[6:18|we have been made servants of justice|servi facti estis justitiæ]] [Denis's text reads *facti estis*, "you have been made"], that is, you are subject to justice, fulfilling the precepts of justice.

paras.t: Sed quia doctrina seu jussio proportionanda est capacitati discipulorum ac subditorum, idcirco infirmis seu imperfectis proponit Apostolus præceptum facile et humanum. Humanum dico, propter infirmitatem carnis vestræ, id est, leve et naturali rationi consonum do vobis præceptum : et hoc, propter vestram imperfectionem et carnis vestræ fragilitatem, propter quæ non potestis præceptum perfectionis seu solidum capere cibum. Deinde ponit præceptum. Sicut enim exhibuistis membra vestra servire immunditiæ, id est carnalibus vitiis, scilicet gulæ, luxuriæ, etc., et iniquitati, id est spiritualibus peccatis, ad iniquitatem, progrediendo de uno peccato in aliud, juxta illud Sapientis : Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum; et illud Apocalypsis, Qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc. Unde per Isaiam ait Scriptura : Væ qui trahitis iniquitatem in funiculis vanitatis, et quasi vinculum plaustri peccatum. Tales sunt perseverantes in malo : quoniam teste Gregorio, peccatum quod statim per pœnitentiam non deletur, suo pondere trahit ad aliud. Ita nunc, agnita veritate, exhibete, id est, præbete et date, membra vestra servire justitiæ, id est virtutibus universis, manibus dando eleemosynam, pedibus eundo ad ecclesiam, oculis peccata deflendo, auribus verbum Dei audiendo, ore Deum laudando, in sanctificationem, id est, vere et plene proficiatis in gratia Dei, in sanctitate et omni perfectione, quemadmodum in Apocalypsi habetur : Sanctus sanctificetur adhuc. Unde per Moysen Dominus præcepit : Sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum Dominus Deus vester : et rursus, Perfectus et absque macula eris cum Domino Deo tuo. — Ecce saluberrimum documentum, rationabilissimumque præceptum, a quo nemo excusare se potest. Quid enim tam vile ac erubescibile, ut quod post nostram conversionem simus pigriores, negligentiores ac frigidiores in obsequio Dei, quam olim eramus in servitute diaboli, carnis et mundi ? Laborandum ergo est nobis, ut vere ac plene convertamus mores nostros. Sed quia hoc adimplere non est volentis neque currentis, sed Dei miserentis, dicamus cum Jeremia : Converte nos, Domine, et convertemur.
paras.en: But since teaching or command must be proportioned to the capacity of disciples and subjects, the Apostle therefore sets before the weak or imperfect an easy and human precept. [[6:19|I speak an human thing, because of the infirmity of your flesh|Humanum dico, propter infirmitatem carnis vestræ]], that is, I give you a light precept, agreeable to natural reason: and this because of your imperfection and the frailty of your flesh, for which you cannot take the precept of perfection, or solid food[[Heb 5:14||]]. Then he gives the precept. [[6:19|For as you have yielded your members to serve uncleanness|Sicut enim exhibuistis membra vestra servire immunditiæ]], that is, carnal vices, namely gluttony, lust, etc., [[6:19|and iniquity|et iniquitati]], that is, spiritual sins, [[6:19|unto iniquity|ad iniquitatem]], going on from one sin to another, according to that of the Wise Man, [[Ecclus 3:29|the sinner will add sin to sin|Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum]]; and that of the Apocalypse, [[Apoc 22:11|he that is filthy, let him be filthy still|Qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc]]. Hence Scripture says through Isaias: [[Is 5:18|Woe to you that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as the rope of a cart|Væ qui trahitis iniquitatem in funiculis vanitatis, et quasi vinculum plaustri peccatum]]. Such are those who persevere in evil: since, as Gregory witnesses, the sin that is not straightway blotted out by penance drags by its weight to another. [[6:19|so now yield your members to serve justice|Ita nunc … exhibete … membra vestra servire justitiæ]], the truth having been known, *yield*, that is, offer and give, that is, to all the virtues: with the hands by giving alms, with the feet by going to church, with the eyes by weeping for sins, with the ears by hearing the word of God, with the mouth by praising God, [[6:19|unto sanctification|in sanctificationem]], that is, that you may truly and fully advance in the grace of God, in holiness and all perfection, as it is in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:11|he that is holy, let him be sanctified still|Sanctus sanctificetur adhuc]]. Hence the Lord commanded through Moses: [[Lev 19:2|Be ye holy, because I the Lord your God am holy|Sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum Dominus Deus vester]]; and again, [[Deut 18:13|Thou shalt be perfect, and without spot before the Lord thy God|Perfectus et absque macula eris cum Domino Deo tuo]]. See a most wholesome lesson and a most reasonable precept, from which no one can excuse himself. For what is so vile and shameful as that after our conversion we should be slower, more negligent and colder in the service of God than we once were in the service of the devil, the flesh and the world? We must labour, then, to change our ways truly and fully. But since to fulfil this [[Rom 9:16|is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy|non est volentis neque currentis, sed Dei miserentis]], let us say with Jeremias: [[Lam 5:21|Convert us, O Lord, to thee, and we shall be converted|Converte nos, Domine, et convertemur]].

paras.t: Quum enim servi essetis peccati, obediendo concupiscentiis et passionibus vestris, liberi fuistis justitiæ, id est, Domino justitiæ caruistis, et spoliati eratis bono justitiæ, atque extranei a rectitudine æquitatis, non obtemperando mandatis divinis : quod veræ libertati maxime derogat. Liberaliter servit, qui voluntatem Domini libenter facit : ideo ad peccandum liber est, qui servus est peccati. Justitiæ quoque libere servit, qui amat et delectatur in ea. Hæc est vera libertas.
paras.en: [[6:20|For when you were the servants of sin|Quum enim servi essetis peccati]], obeying your lusts and passions, [[6:20|you were free men to justice|liberi fuistis justitiæ]], that is, you lacked the Lord of justice, and were stripped of the good of justice and strangers to the rightness of equity, not obeying the divine commandments: which most of all takes away from true freedom. He serves freely who does his Lord's will gladly: therefore he who is the servant of sin is free for sinning. And he serves justice freely who loves it and delights in it. This is true freedom.

paras.t: Quem ergo fructum, id est profectum seu utilitatem, habuistis tunc in illis, quando scelerate vixistis, in quibus nunc erubescitis, id est in actibus vitiosis ac turpibus, de quorum perpetratione verecundamini modo, ad Deum conversi atque divinitus illustrati, ac per hoc inhonestatem peccati agnoscentes ? Peccator namque, post suam conversionem, erubescit de malis in quibus aliquando gloriabatur, quemadmodum scriptum est : Erubescite, et confundimini super viis vestris, dicit Dominus. Nam finis, id est merces finalis, illorum turpium vitiorum, mors est, id est æterna damnatio. Vel, mors ista temporalis, est finis, id est terminus, illorum, quia post mortem hanc non possunt impii talia agere : propter quod eorum delectatio brevis est. Nunc vero liberati a peccato, per Christi passionem, tanquam per causam meritoriam universalem, per propriam quoque pœnitentiam seu Baptismum, tanquam per causam meritoriam particularem, per gratiæ autem infusionem formaliter, servi autem facti Deo, obediendo ejus præceptis, seu acquiescendo ejus consiliis, habetis fructum vestrum, id est profectum seu perfectionem vobis congruentem, in sanctificationem animarum vestrarum, ita quod fructus iste est sanctificatio vestra, seu puritas animæ. Unde ait Dominus : Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt. Finem vero, id est finale consummatumque præmium, habetis vitam æternam, quæ erit tota merces vestra. Ad hunc fructum seu cordis puritatem omnia exercere debemus, semper solliciti coram divino conspectu habere cor mundum : in quo, scilicet in habendo cor mundum, consistit summa viæ hujus perfectio, quia ut Salomon ait, Qui diligit cordis munditiam, amicum habebit regem. Vita autem æterna, quæ est visio Dei in patria, est finis ultimatus : ad quem etiam ipsa puritas animæ viatricis disponit ac ordinatur.
paras.en: [[6:21|What fruit therefore|Quem ergo fructum]], that is, profit or advantage, [[6:21|had you then in those things|habuistis tunc in illis]], when you lived wickedly, [[6:21|of which you are now ashamed?|in quibus nunc erubescitis]], that is, in vicious and shameful acts, of whose committing you are now ashamed, being converted to God and enlightened from above, and so knowing the foulness of sin? For the sinner, after his conversion, is ashamed of the evils in which he once gloried, as it is written: [[Ezech 36:32|be confounded, and ashamed at your own ways|Erubescite, et confundimini super viis vestris]], saith the Lord. [[6:21|For the end|Nam finis]], that is, the final wages, [[6:21|of them|illorum]], the shameful vices, [[6:21|is death|mors est]], that is, eternal damnation. Or, this temporal death is the end, that is, the term, of them, because after this death the wicked cannot do such things: for which reason their delight is short. [[6:22|But now being made free from sin|Nunc vero liberati a peccato]] by Christ's passion, as by the universal meritorious cause, and by your own penance or Baptism, as by a particular meritorious cause, and formally by the infusion of grace, [[6:22|and become servants to God|servi autem facti Deo]], obeying his precepts, or following his counsels, [[6:22|you have your fruit|habetis fructum vestrum]], that is, the profit or perfection fitting for you, [[6:22|unto sanctification|in sanctificationem]] of your souls, so that this fruit is your sanctification, or purity of soul. Hence the Lord says: [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]]. [[6:22|and the end|Finem vero]], that is, the final and complete reward, [[6:22|life everlasting|vitam æternam]], you have, which will be your whole reward. To this fruit, or purity of heart, we must direct everything, ever careful to have a clean heart in the sight of God: in which, namely in having a clean heart, consists the highest perfection of this way, since, as Solomon says, [[Prov 22:11|He that loveth cleanness of heart, for the grace of his lips shall have the king for his friend|Qui diligit cordis munditiam, amicum habebit regem]]. And eternal life, which is the vision of God in the fatherland, is the last end: to which the very purity of the soul on its way disposes and is ordered.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Apostolus, quod finis illorum, utpote vitiorum, est mors atque damnatio animæ. Stipendia enim peccati, id est retributio debita quæ pro peccato infligitur, est mors temporalis et æterna. Ex originali enim peccato processit mors corporalis, in pœnam illius peccati. Propter quod legitur in libro Sapientiæ : Deus mortem non fecit; invidia autem diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum. Pro peccato autem actuali mortali infligitur mors æterna, quæ utique est a Deo, quum sit justa pœna, sicut scriptum est : Mors et vita ab ipso […] sunt. Gratia autem Dei, id est ex gratia seu per gratiam Dei, datur justis pro præmio vita æterna.
