Non hoc dicitur, merita excludendo, sed ut insinuetur quod principaliter adscribendum sit gratiæ Dei, qui etiam præmiat ultra condignum. Electi enim per gratiam merentur vitam æternam. Unde tam meritum quam præmium nostrum, primo et maxime dependet atque procedit ex pietate Dei, et gratia ejus quam efficit in nobis. Hæc autem vita æterna est in Christo Jesu Domino nostro, tanquam in objecto et causa effectiva principali, secundum divinam ejus naturam, sicut in Patre et Spiritu Sancto. Tota enim superbenedicta Trinitas, est causa efficiens et objectum vitæ æternæ, id est beatitudinis electorum. Porro in Jesu Christo, id est per eum, datur nobis gratiose vita æterna, quia sicut jam sæpius dixi, omnia dona nobis per Christum hominem conferuntur.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows that the end of those things, namely of vices, is the death and damnation of the soul. [[6:23|For the wages of sin|Stipendia enim peccati]], that is, the due retribution inflicted for sin, [[6:23|is death|mors]], temporal and eternal. For from original sin came bodily death, as the punishment of that sin. For which reason we read in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 1:13|For God made not death|Deus mortem non fecit]]; [[Wis 2:24|But by the envy of the devil, death came into the world|invidia autem diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum]]. And for actual mortal sin eternal death is inflicted, which indeed is from God, since it is a just punishment, as it is written: [[Ecclus 11:14|life and death, poverty and riches, are from God|et mala, vita et mors, paupertas et honestas, a Deo sunt]] […]. [[6:23|But the grace of God|Gratia autem Dei]], that is, from grace or by the grace of God, is given to the just as reward [[6:23|life everlasting|vita æterna]]. This is not said to exclude merits, but to suggest that it is to be ascribed principally to the grace of God, who also rewards beyond what is deserved. For the elect merit eternal life through grace. Hence both our merit and our reward depend and proceed first and chiefly from the loving-kindness of God, and the grace which he works in us. And this [[6:23|life everlasting|vita æterna]] is [[6:23|in Christ Jesus our Lord|in Christo Jesu Domino nostro]], as in its object and principal effective cause, according to his divine nature, as in the Father and the Holy Ghost. For the whole superblessed Trinity is the efficient cause and the object of eternal life, that is, of the beatitude of the elect. Further, in Jesus Christ, that is, through him, eternal life is given us graciously, since, as I have often said already, all gifts are conferred on us through Christ the man.

8.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI OCTAVI : NIHIL ERGO NUNC DAMNATIONIS EST, ETC.
8.title_en: Explanation of the eighth chapter: There is now therefore no condemnation, etc.

paras.t: DECLARATA in præcedenti capitulo cessatione legis Mosaicæ, jam docet Christo et evangelicæ legi jugiter inhærendum, et ait : Nihil ergo nunc, scilicet tempore gratiæ, damnationis, id est obligationis ad pœnam gehennæ, est his qui sunt in Christo Jesu per fidem et caritatem : quibus ipse loquitur, Manete in me, et ego in vobis ; qui non secundum carnem ambulant, id est, carnis desideriis non acquiescunt, neque carnaliter vivunt, sed carnem cum vitiis et concupiscentiis crucifigunt. In fonte namque Baptismatis dimissa sunt eis peccata universa. Si autem postea non peccaverunt, manendo in Christo proferunt fructum multum, et ita non tantum pro vitiis satisfaciunt, sed insuper gloriam ampliorem merentur. Lex enim spiritus vitæ, id est lex evangelica : quæ nominatur lex spiritus, quia a Spiritu Sancto est data, Christianorumque cordibus ab ipso impressa; dicitur quoque lex vitæ, quoniam mentem vivificat, per gratiam quam sacramenta novæ legis distribuunt; in Christo Jesu, id est per Christum, liberavit me a lege peccati et mortis, id est a consensu, consuetudine, et actu culpæ ac pœnæ pro culpa infligendæ. Potest quoque per legem peccati, lex scripta intelligi, eo quod ex occasione auxerit culpam ac pœnam, quemadmodum in superioribus ubertim expositum est.
paras.en: Having in the preceding chapter set forth the ceasing of the Mosaic law, he now teaches that we must cleave constantly to Christ and to the law of the Gospel, and says: [[8:1|There is now therefore|Nihil ergo nunc]], that is, in the time of grace, [[8:1|no condemnation|damnationis]], that is, no liability to the punishment of hell, [[8:1|to them that are in Christ Jesus|est his qui sunt in Christo Jesu]] by faith and charity: to whom He Himself says, [[John 15:4|Abide in me: and I in you|Manete in me, et ego in vobis]]; [[8:1|who walk not according to the flesh|qui non secundum carnem ambulant]], that is, who do not yield to the desires of the flesh nor live carnally, but crucify the flesh with its vices and concupiscences[[Gal 5:24||]]. For in the font of Baptism all their sins were forgiven them. And if afterwards they have not sinned, by abiding in Christ they bring forth much fruit[[John 15:5||]], and so not only make satisfaction for their faults, but moreover merit greater glory. [[8:2|For the law of the spirit of life|Lex enim spiritus vitæ]], that is, the law of the Gospel: which is called the law of the spirit because it was given by the Holy Ghost and imprinted by Him on the hearts of Christians; and it is called the law of life because it quickens the mind through the grace which the sacraments of the new law dispense; [[8:2|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through Christ, [[8:2|hath delivered me from the law of sin and of death|liberavit me a lege peccati et mortis]], that is, from the consent, the habit and the act of guilt, and from the punishment to be inflicted for guilt. By the law of sin may also be understood the written law, in that it occasionally increased guilt and punishment, as was set forth at length above[[Rom 7:8||]].

paras.t: Proinde declarat Apostolus, quomodo lex Christi, quæ est lex spiritus vitæ, liberet a lege peccati et mortis. Nam quod impossibile erat legi scriptæ et sacramentis ipsius, non continentibus nec conferentibus gratiam, in quo infirmabatur, id est, in qua impossibilitate atque inefficacia, infirma et ad salvandum impotens erat lex ipsa, per carnem, id est per observantias et justificationes carnales, quæ non purificant animam. Sacramenta enim legalia corporaliter tantum mundabant, quasdam inhabilitates seu irregularitates ab exteriori inductas, et ab ingressu templi atque similibus impedientes, tollendo. Vel, Per carnem, id est per fomitem carnis, quem lex occasionaliter incitavit, non directe diminuit. Deus Pater Filium suum mittens in mundum per incarnationis mysterium, non per localem descensum, in similitudinem carnis peccati, id est in corpore mortali atque passibili : quod licet fuerit veraciter veraque caro, non tamen veraciter erat caro peccati, sed similitudinarie. Per pœnas enim quas pertulit, similis erat carni peccatrici. Venit itaque Christus in veritate carnis, non autem in veritate carnis peccati, sed in similitudine ejus.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows how the law of Christ, which is the law of the spirit of life, delivers from the law of sin and of death. [[8:3|For what the law could not do|Nam quod impossibile erat legi]], the written law and its sacraments, which neither contained nor conferred grace, [[8:3|in that it was weak|in quo infirmabatur]], that is, in which impossibility and inefficacy the law itself was weak and powerless to save, [[8:3|through the flesh|per carnem]], that is, through carnal observances and justifications, which do not purify the soul. For the legal sacraments cleansed only bodily, by removing certain disabilities or irregularities contracted from without, which barred from entering the temple and the like. Or, through the flesh, that is, through the fomes of the flesh [the inclination to sin left in fallen nature], which the law occasionally stirred up and did not directly lessen. [[8:3|God, sending his own Son|Deus Pater Filium suum mittens]] (God the Father) into the world through the mystery of the Incarnation, not by a descent in place, [[8:3|in the likeness of sinful flesh|in similitudinem carnis peccati]], that is, in a mortal and passible body: which, though it was truly and really flesh, was not truly flesh of sin, but only by likeness. For through the penalties which He bore He was like to sinful flesh. Christ therefore came in the reality of flesh, but not in the reality of sinful flesh, only in its likeness.

paras.t: Et de peccato damnavit peccatum : id est, Pater mittens sic Filium, damnavit, id est, delevit, destruxit, dimisit peccatum, tam originale quam actuale, de peccato, id est per peccatum factum in carne Christi, non a Christo, sed a diabolo ejusque ministris qui Christum occiderunt. Per hoc enim quod Christus injuste occisus est, suggerente diabolo, amisit diabolus jus quod habebat in nobis, et ita mors Christo inique illata, omne peccatum delevit. Vel : Damnavit peccatum actuale, nascens de peccato, id est fomite peccati ; vel, Peccatum de peccato, id est fomitem peccati, procedentem de peccato originali Adæ. Vel sic, et melius, secundum Ambrosium : De peccato, id est de se ipso, prout factus est hostia pro peccato nostro, damnavit, id est delevit, peccatum mundi quodcumque, in carne, id est in corporis sui passione. Ipse enim portavit peccata nostra in corpore suo super lignum. Juxta hunc sensum sacrificia legis pro peccatis oblata, dicebantur peccata, secundum quod de sacerdotibus veteris Testamenti Dominus ait per Osee : Peccata populi mei comedent. Sic quoque aquam cum periculo vitæ allatam David, sanguinem appellavit, dicens : Absit a me, ut sanguinem virorum istorum bibam.
paras.en: [[8:3|and of sin, hath condemned sin|et de peccato, damnavit peccatum]]: that is, the Father, sending the Son thus, condemned, that is, blotted out, destroyed, remitted sin, original as well as actual, of sin, that is, by the sin committed [[8:3|in the flesh|in carne]] of Christ, not by Christ, but by the devil and his ministers who slew Christ. For because Christ was unjustly slain at the devil's prompting, the devil lost the right he had over us, and so the death wickedly inflicted on Christ blotted out all sin. Or: He condemned actual sin, springing of sin, that is, of the fomes of sin; or, sin of sin, that is, the fomes of sin proceeding from the original sin of Adam. Or thus, and better, according to Ambrose: Of sin, that is, of Himself, inasmuch as He was made a victim for our sin, He condemned, that is, blotted out, every sin of the world, in the flesh, that is, in the passion of His body. For [[1 Pet 2:24|Who his own self bore our sins in his body upon the tree|Ipse … portavit … super lignum]]. In this sense the sacrifices of the law offered for sins were called sins, as the Lord says through Osee of the priests of the Old Testament: [[Osee 4:8|They shall eat the sins of my people|Peccata populi mei comedent]] [Denis's word order differs slightly from the Vulgate]. So too David called the water brought at peril of life blood, saying: [[1 Par 11:19|God forbid that I should do this in the sight of my God, and should drink the blood of these men|Absit a me, ut sanguinem virorum istorum bibam]].

paras.t: Hæc itaque fecit Deus, ut justificatio legis, id est in lege promissa, non autem per legem exhibita : lex enim gratiam justificantem spopondit, non contulit: impleretur in nobis, qui in Baptismo aliisque sacramentis gratiam justificantem in lege præfiguratam ac prænuntiatam recipimus, qui non secundum carnem ambulamus, sed secundum spiritum, id est, non carnaliter, sed spiritualiter in hujus vitæ exsilio conversamur, tendentes ac properantes ad patriam per opera virtuosa. De hac legis promissione aiebat Apostolus loquens de Judæis : Et nos vobis annuntiamus eam quæ ad patres nostros facta est repromissio, quoniam hanc Deus implevit filiis nostris. Hinc etiam Petrus in sua Canonica : De qua salute exquisierunt atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui de futura in vobis gratia prophetaverunt : quibus revelatum est quia non sibi ipsis, vobis autem ministraverunt ea quæ nunc nuntiata sunt vobis.
paras.en: These things, then, God did [[8:4|That the justification of the law|ut justificatio legis]], that is, promised in the law, but not bestowed through the law (for the law promised justifying grace but did not confer it), [[8:4|might be fulfilled in us|impleretur in nobis]], who in Baptism and the other sacraments receive the justifying grace prefigured and foretold in the law, [[8:4|who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit|qui non secundum carnem ambulamus, sed secundum spiritum]], that is, who live in the exile of this life not carnally but spiritually, tending and hastening to the fatherland by virtuous works. Of this promise of the law the Apostle said, speaking of the Jews: [[Acts 13:32|And we declare unto you that the promise which was made|Et nos vobis annuntiamus eam quæ ad patres nostros facta est]], [[Acts 13:33|This same God hath fulfilled to our children|quoniam hanc Deus implevit filiis nostris]]. Hence also Peter in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 1:10|Of which salvation the prophets have inquired and diligently searched, who prophesied of the grace to come in you|De qua salute exquisierunt atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui de futura in vobis]] [[1 Pet 1:12|To whom it was revealed that, not to themselves but to you, they ministered those things which are now declared to you|quibus revelatum est quia non sibi ipsis, vobis autem ministraverunt ea quæ nunc nuntiata sunt vobis]].

paras.t: Pro intellectu loci hujus intricati atque difficilis advertendum, quod nemo unquam salvatus est nisi per fidem et gratiam Christi. Ipse enim est caput omnium electorum ; membra autem necesse est capiti counire, ut vitam participent. Propter quod Petrus disserebat : Nec enim aliud nomen sub cœlo datum est hominibus, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri. Passio namque Christi hoc fecit futura, quod facit impleta.
paras.en: For the understanding of this intricate and difficult passage, note that no one was ever saved except through faith in Christ and His grace. For He is the head of all the elect[[Eph 1:22||]]; and the members must be united to the head in order to share its life. Wherefore Peter declared: [[Acts 4:12|For there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved|Nec enim aliud nomen sub cœlo datum est hominibus, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri]]. For the passion of Christ, while yet to come, did the same as it does now accomplished.

paras.t: Porro, hæc salus aliter applicatur hominibus post Christi passionem, et aliter ante. Tunc enim applicabatur per fidem formatam, nunc vero applicatur etiam per sacramenta gratiæ contentiva, effectiva et causativa. Potest autem aliquid movere vel agere, antequam sit in effectu, videlicet secundum quod est in apprehensione animæ, et dispositione causæ efficientis, quemadmodum finis movet agentem. Ad hoc autem quod aliquid agat et moveat in genere causæ efficientis, oportet ut sit, et effectum præcedat, eo quod causa effectiva non sit suo effectu posterior. Sacramenta ergo veteris legis et fides Christi venturi, habere non poterant quemlibet effectum dominicæ passionis, quem nunc habent sacramenta ac fides evangelicæ legis, quæ operantur virtute passionis dominicæ jam impletæ. Et ideo gratiam operantur, et a reatu originalis peccati absolvunt : quorum nullum sacramenta legis facere poterant. Unde omnes patres pro tunc descenderunt in limbum inferni. Nam licet per fidem et gratiam Dei, virtute passionis Christi et merito ejus futuro, absolverentur a pœna et culpa actualium peccatorum, non tamen a reatu originalis peccati.
paras.en: Now this salvation is applied to men in one way after Christ's passion and in another before it. Then it was applied through formed faith [that is, faith informed by charity]; now it is applied also through sacraments which contain, effect and cause grace. A thing can move or act before it exists in fact, namely inasmuch as it is in the apprehension of the mind and in the intention of the efficient cause, as the end moves the agent. But for a thing to act and move in the order of efficient cause, it must exist and precede the effect, since an efficient cause is not later than its effect. The sacraments of the old law, therefore, and faith in Christ to come, could not have every effect of the Lord's passion which the sacraments and faith of the Gospel law now have, which work by the power of the Lord's passion already accomplished. And so these work grace and absolve from the guilt of original sin, neither of which the sacraments of the law could do. Hence all the fathers of that time went down into the limbo of hell. For although through faith and the grace of God, by the power of Christ's passion and His merit yet to come, they were absolved from the punishment and guilt of actual sins, they were not absolved from the guilt of original sin.

paras.t: Ex quo innotescit, quod passio Christi fortius agit impleta, quam egit implenda. Quemadmodum enim sacramenta novæ legis, sunt causæ instrumentales nostræ salutis et gratiæ, quoniam agunt virtute et merito passionis dominicæ, suntque vasa medicinalia spiritualium unguentorum contentiva, animarum languores curantia ; sic humanitas seu passio Christi, est causa instrumentalis, effectiva et meritoria nostræ salutis et gratiæ. Utrumque vero est instrumentum divinitatis Christi. Divinitas namque est causa efficiens principalis, quæ agit per humanitatem assumptam sicut per instrumentum conjunctum, per sacramenta vero, sicut per instrumenta separata : quemadmodum medicus est causa sanitatis efficiens principalis, manus autem est sicut causa instrumentalis conjuncta, ignis vero quo medicina paratur, est causa instrumentalis separata. Causa autem instrumentalis quum est in effectu, vel quum causa ejus principalis jam est, fortius operatur quam ante. Hinc ergo ait Apostolus, quod Deus misit Filium suum, de peccato damnans peccatum, ut justificatio legis impleretur in nobis : quod impossibile erat legi, justificare non valenti, in quo lex infirmabatur, seu debilis erat. Et hoc modo construenda est littera.
paras.en: From this it appears that the passion of Christ acts more powerfully now accomplished than it acted when yet to be accomplished. For as the sacraments of the new law are instrumental causes of our salvation and grace, since they act by the power and merit of the Lord's passion, and are medicinal vessels containing spiritual ointments that heal the sicknesses of souls; so the humanity or passion of Christ is the instrumental, effective and meritorious cause of our salvation and grace. Both are instruments of the Godhead of Christ. For the Godhead is the principal efficient cause, acting through the assumed humanity as through a conjoined instrument, and through the sacraments as through separate instruments: as the physician is the principal efficient cause of health, the hand as a conjoined instrumental cause, and the fire with which the medicine is prepared a separate instrumental cause. And an instrumental cause, when it exists in fact, or when its principal cause already exists, works more powerfully than before. Hence the Apostle says that God sent His Son, condemning sin of sin, that the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us: which was impossible to the law, which could not justify, in which the law was weak or feeble. And in this way the text is to be construed.

paras.t: Quod autem justificatio legis non nisi in spiritualibus impleatur hominibus, liquet. Qui enim secundum carnem sunt, id est, qui carnaliter vivunt : qui utique attendunt se ipsos secundum esse suum carnale ac sensitivum, non secundum esse spirituale ac intellectivum ; quæ carnis sunt, sapiunt, id est, carnalia gustant, sensibilia ac temporalia cum sensualitatis sapore attendunt. Qui vero secundum spiritum, id est spiritualiter conversantes, et esse suum supremum, in quo Trinitatis imago relucet, pensantes, quæ sunt spiritus sentiunt, id est, spiritualia atque divina saporose intelligunt, delectabiliter pensant, sollicite implent, in talibus jugiter occupantur.
paras.en: That the justification of the law is fulfilled only in spiritual men is plain. [[8:5|For they that are according to the flesh|Qui enim secundum carnem sunt]], that is, who live carnally, who regard themselves according to their carnal and sensitive being, not according to their spiritual and intellectual being, [[8:5|mind the things that are of the flesh|quæ carnis sunt, sapiunt]], that is, relish carnal things, attend to sensible and temporal things with the savour of sensuality [the Latin *sapiunt*, “mind”, is akin to *sapor*, taste]. [[8:5|but they that are according to the spirit|Qui vero secundum spiritum]], that is, those who live spiritually and ponder their highest being, in which the image of the Trinity shines, [[8:5|mind the things that are of the spirit|quæ sunt spiritus, sentiunt]], that is, understand spiritual and divine things with relish, ponder them with delight, carry them out with care, and are constantly occupied in them.

paras.t: Nam prudentia carnis, id est carnalis ac sæcularis prudentia, mors est, id est mortale peccatum, inferens mortem culpæ in via, mortemque pœnæ in gehenna. Dicitur autem prudentia carnis hoc loco, per quam homo sibi in bonis carnalibus ac mundanis finem constituit, et ad talis finis adeptionem opera sua caute disponit. Hæc prudentia, non est vera prudentia, sed appellatur prudentia, propter apparentem similitudinem quam habet cum vera prudentia. Unde ait Salvator : Filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis in generatione sua sunt ; et Jacobus, Non est ista sapientia (id est prudentia) a Deo, sed terrena, animalis et diabolica. Prudentia autem spiritus, id est vera ac spiritualis prudentia, quæ opera hominis convenienter disponit in ordine ad ultimum finem, est vita et pax, id est causa vitæ et pacis, in præsenti inchoative, in futuro perfecte. Nunc enim efficit in nobis vitam pacemque gratiæ, in patria vero meretur, vel potius adipiscitur, pacem et vitam gloriæ. Non distinguit Apostolus jam inter prudentiam et sapientiam. Proprie enim ad sapientiam spectat spiritualia sapere. De hac ergo spirituali prudentia, intelligendum est illud Jacobi : Quæ desursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suasibilis, bonis consentiens. Sciendum quoque quod pax directe ac proprie, est caritatis effectus, juxta illud in Psalmo : Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam. Est etiam pax effectus justitiæ, tanquam removentis impedimenta pacis. Propter quod per Isaiam dicitur : Erit opus justitiæ pax. Nunc vero dicitur pax esse effectus prudentiæ, tanquam dirigentis affectus nostros in viam pacis.
paras.en: [[8:6|For the wisdom of the flesh|Nam prudentia carnis]] [the Latin has *prudentia*, prudence], that is, carnal and worldly prudence, [[8:6|is death|mors est]], that is, mortal sin, bringing the death of guilt on the way and the death of punishment in hell. Here prudence of the flesh means that by which a man sets his end in carnal and worldly goods and cunningly orders his works to the attaining of such an end. This is not true prudence, but is called prudence because of its apparent likeness to true prudence. Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 16:8|the children of this world are wiser in their generation than the children of light|Filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis in generatione sua sunt]]; and James: [[Jas 3:15|For this is not wisdom|Non est ista sapientia]] (that is, prudence) [[Jas 3:15|descending from above: but earthly, sensual, devilish|a Deo, sed terrena, animalis et diabolica]]. [[8:6|but the wisdom of the spirit|Prudentia autem spiritus]], that is, true and spiritual prudence, which fitly orders a man's works to the last end, is [[8:6|life and peace|vita et pax]], that is, the cause of life and peace, begun in the present, perfect in the future. For now it works in us the life and peace of grace, and in the fatherland it merits, or rather attains, the peace and life of glory. The Apostle here does not distinguish between prudence and wisdom, though properly it belongs to wisdom to savour spiritual things. Of this spiritual prudence, then, is to be understood that saying of James: [[Jas 3:17|But the wisdom that is from above, first indeed is chaste, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good|Quæ desursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suasibilis, bonis consentiens]]. Know too that peace is directly and properly the effect of charity, according to the Psalm: [[Ps 118:165|Much peace have they that love thy law|Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam]]. Peace is also the effect of justice, as removing the hindrances of peace; wherefore it is said through Isaias: [[Is 32:17|And the work of justice shall be peace|Erit opus justitiæ pax]]. Here peace is said to be the effect of prudence, as directing our affections into the way of peace.

paras.t: Quoniam sapientia carnis inimica est Deo, id est divinæ voluntati atque sapientiæ veræ contraria. Ecce nunc loco prudentiæ ponit sapientiam : ex quo certum est, quod inter sapientiam et prudentiam non distinguit. Legi enim Dei non est subjecta sapientia ista carnalis, mundana ac vana, quia nec credit nec agit quæ lex divina tradit esse credenda sive agenda. Propter quod ait Salvator : Confiteor tibi, Pater, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis ; et Jeremias, Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt. Nec enim potest divinæ legi esse subjecta sapientia ista. Unum namque oppositorum non subjicitur alteri, sed repugnat. Lex autem divina docet ultimum finem esse constituendum in Deo, hæc vero in bonis carnalibus. Qui autem in carne sunt, id est, carnaliter vivunt, atque in sensibilibus bonis finaliter sistunt, Deo placere non possunt, in quantum hujusmodi. Possunt tamen converti, et Deo reconciliari. Huic dicto consonat illud Salvatoris : Nemo potest duobus dominis servire.
paras.en: [[8:7|Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God|Quoniam sapientia carnis inimica est Deo]], that is, contrary to the divine will and to true wisdom. See, he now puts wisdom in place of prudence; whence it is certain that he does not distinguish between them. [[8:7|For it is not subject to the law of God|Legi enim Dei non est subjecta]], this carnal, worldly and vain wisdom, because it neither believes nor does what the divine law teaches must be believed or done. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[Luke 10:21|I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent and hast revealed them to little ones|Confiteor tibi, Pater, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]; and Jeremias: [[Jer 4:22|they are wise to do evil, but to do good|Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt]]. [[8:7|neither can it be|Nec enim potest]] subject to the divine law, this wisdom. For one of two opposites is not subject to the other but resists it. The divine law teaches that the last end is to be placed in God, this wisdom places it in carnal goods. [[8:8|And they who are in the flesh|Qui autem in carne sunt]], that is, who live carnally and rest finally in sensible goods, [[8:8|cannot please God|Deo placere non possunt]], insofar as they are such. Yet they can be converted and reconciled to God. With this saying agrees that of the Saviour: [[Matt 6:24|No man can serve two masters|Nemo potest duobus dominis servire]].

paras.t: Vos autem, o veraciter Christifideles, in carne non estis, id est, in rebus ac vitiis carnis non detinemini, sed spiritualia atque divina exquiritis, conversationem habentes in cœlis, sed in spiritu, id est, in Spiritu Sancto estis, per caritatem et gratiam, et propter spiritualem regenerationem, qua estis ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto renati. Vel, Estis in spiritu vestro, id est secundum rationis judicium vivitis : juxta quod scriptum est, Redite, prævaricatores, ad cor. Si tamen Spiritus Dei, id est Spiritus Sanctus, habitat, id est manet, in vobis per gratiam gratum facientem : quemadmodum loquitur Christus, Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum. Rursusque ait : Spiritus Sanctus apud vos manebit, et in vobis erit. Si quis autem Spiritum Christi non habet, id est, cujus anima non habitatur a Spiritu Sancto : qui est Spiritus Christi, quia ab ipso procedit, ab eoque datur ac mittitur, sicut ipse protestatur. Quum venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis a Patre : et iterum, Ille de meo accipiet. Et ad hoc designandum, insufflavit in discipulos suos, et dixit : Accipite Spiritum Sanctum. Quis autem habet Spiritum Sanctum, nisi quietus et humilis, simplex et justus? Scriptum est enim : Super quem requiescet Spiritus meus, nisi super quietum et humilem? Et iterum : Spiritus Sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu. Hic non est ejus, id est, ad membra Christi non pertinet, secundum præsentem justitiam et merito, quamvis interdum pertineat secundum prædestinationem æternam ac numero, sicut et Paulus quum Stephanum lapidavit.
paras.en: [[8:9|But you are not in the flesh|Vos autem in carne non estis]], O truly faithful of Christ, that is, you are not held fast in the things and vices of the flesh, but seek spiritual and divine things, having your conversation in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], [[8:9|but the spirit|sed in spiritu]], that is, you are in the Holy Ghost, by charity and grace, and by the spiritual regeneration whereby you are born again of water and the Holy Ghost[[John 3:5||]]. Or, you are in your own spirit, that is, you live according to the judgement of reason, as it is written: [[Is 46:8|return, ye transgressors, to the heart|Redite, prævaricatores, ad cor]]. [[8:9|if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you|Si tamen Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis]], that is, the Holy Ghost abides in you through sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God]: as Christ says, [[John 14:16|And I will ask the Father: and he shall give you another Paraclete, that he may abide with you for ever|Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum]]. And again He says: [[John 14:17|he shall abide with you and shall be in you|apud vos manebit, et in vobis erit]] [Denis supplies “the Holy Ghost” as subject]. [[8:9|Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ|Si quis autem Spiritum Christi non habet]], that is, whose soul is not indwelt by the Holy Ghost, who is the Spirit of Christ because He proceeds from Him and is given and sent by Him, as He Himself declares: [[John 15:26|But when the Paraclete cometh, whom I will send you from the Father|Quum venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis a Patre]] [the margin gives John xv, 26]; and again: [[John 16:14|he shall receive of mine|Ille de meo accipiet]]. And to signify this He breathed on His disciples and said: [[John 20:22|Receive ye the Holy Ghost|Accipite Spiritum Sanctum]]. But who has the Holy Ghost save the quiet and humble, the simple and just? For it is written: Upon whom shall my Spirit rest, but upon the quiet and the humble?[[Is 66:2||]] [the Vulgate reads differently: “to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little”]. And again: [[Wis 1:5|For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw himself from thoughts that are without understanding|Spiritus Sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu]]. [[8:9|he is none of his|Hic non est ejus]], that is, he does not belong to the members of Christ according to present justice and by merit, though at times he belongs to them according to eternal predestination and in number, as Paul did when he stoned Stephen[[Acts 7:57||]].

paras.t: Deinde pandit Apostolus, quid utilitatis consequantur fideles ex inhabitatione Spiritus Sancti. Si autem Christus in vobis est, per fidem et caritatem : sicut et alibi legitur, Christum per fidem habitare in cordibus vestris; et Salvator ipse, Ego, inquit, vobiscum sum cunctis diebus ; corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum, id est, caro vestra mortalis ac fragilis, necessitati moriendi subjecta est propter originale peccatum, spiritus vero, id est anima vestra, vivit per gratiam, propter justificationem sibi a Christo collatam, id est per hoc quod peccata ei dimissa sunt, quæ spiritum vulnerabant. Vel, Propter justificationem, id est per justitiæ exercitationem. Bona enim operatio, vita est animæ. Hinc ait Salvator : Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant.
paras.en: Then the Apostle shows what benefit the faithful gain from the indwelling of the Holy Ghost. [[8:10|And if Christ be in you|Si autem Christus in vobis est]] by faith and charity, as is read elsewhere, [[Eph 3:17|That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts|Christum per fidem habitare in cordibus vestris]]; and the Saviour Himself says, [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days|Ego … vobiscum sum … diebus]]; [[8:10|the body indeed is dead, because of sin|corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum]], that is, your mortal and frail flesh is subject to the necessity of dying because of original sin, [[8:10|but the spirit liveth|spiritus vero vivit]], that is, your soul lives by grace, [[8:10|because of justification|propter justificationem]] conferred on it by Christ, that is, because the sins which wounded the spirit have been forgiven it. Or, because of justification, that is, through the exercise of justice; for good works are the life of the soul. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 10:10|I am come that they may have life and may have it more abundantly|Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant]].

paras.t: Quod si Spiritus ejus, id est Spiritus Dei Patris, qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis, habitat in vobis perseveranter usque in finem vitæ præsentis, ita ut in gratia decedatis; qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis, scilicet Deus Pater, vivificabit, id est, ad immortalem vitam resuscitabit, et mortalia corpora vestra in die novissimo : sicut Job apertissime profitetur : Credo quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum, et rursum circumdabor pelle mea. Per Isaiam quoque Dominus asserit : Vivent mortui tui, interfectique mei resurgent. Propter inhabitantem Spiritum ejus in vobis, id est virtute et gratia Spiritus Sancti; vel, propter benignitatem qua fecit Spiritum Sanctum habitare in mentibus vestris; vel, propter meritum quod consecuti estis ex inhabitatione et gratia Spiritus Sancti : imo, propter utrumque istorum simul, videlicet propter misericordiam Dei et opera vestra bona, suscitabuntur corpora vestra ad beatam et impassibilem vitam.
paras.en: [[8:11|And if the Spirit of him|Quod si Spiritus ejus]], that is, the Spirit of God the Father, [[8:11|that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you|qui suscitavit Jesum a mortuis, habitat in vobis]] perseveringly to the end of the present life, so that you depart in grace; [[8:11|he that raised up Jesus Christ, from the dead|qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis]], namely God the Father, [[8:11|shall quicken|vivificabit]], that is, shall raise to immortal life, [[8:11|also your mortal bodies|et mortalia corpora vestra]] on the last day: as Job most openly professes: [[Job 19:25|For I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Credo quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]] [[Job 19:26|And I shall be clothed again with my skin|et rursum circumdabor pelle mea]]. Through Isaias also the Lord declares: [[Is 26:19|Thy dead men shall live, my slain shall rise again|Vivent mortui tui, interfectique mei resurgent]]. [[8:11|because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you|propter inhabitantem Spiritum ejus in vobis]], that is, by the power and grace of the Holy Ghost; or, because of the kindness by which He made the Holy Ghost dwell in your minds; or, because of the merit you have gained from the indwelling and grace of the Holy Ghost: nay rather, for both of these together, namely for God's mercy and your good works, your bodies shall be raised to a blessed and impassible life.

paras.t: Ex prædictis infert Apostolus, quod fideles obtemperare tenentur rationi, non sensualitati : spiritui, non carni. Ergo, o fratres, debitores sumus non carni, ut secundum carnem vivamus : id est, quamvis aliquo modo obligemur carni, videlicet ut ei necessaria ministremus in victu atque vestitu, non tamen sic ei obligati sumus, ut ejus concupiscentiis acquiescamus, carnaliterque vivamus. Si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini, morte culpæ in hoc sæculo, et morte perpetua in inferno. Si autem spiritu, id est gratia Spiritus Sancti; vel, Spiritu, id est rationis vestræ judicio ; facta, id est opera, carnis mortificaveritis, id est, destruxeritis et abjeceritis tanquam venena : quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico præcipitur, Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum ; vivetis, vita caritatis et gratiæ in Ecclesia militanti, vita quoque fruitionis et gloriæ in Ecclesia triumphanti. Huic documento naturalis consonat ratio. Media namque disponenda sunt secundum exigentiam finis. Quum ergo caro sit animæ instrumentum, et ordinetur ad spiritum sicut ad finem, regenda est secundum exigentiam animæ seu spiritus, scilicet, ut animæ serviat, rationi obediat, illisque actibus occupetur per quæ spiritus tendit et redit ad Creatorem. Qui autem secundum carnem conversatur, pervertit hunc ordinem, dominam ancillæ subjiciens, finem medio postponens, et se ipsum bestiis viliorem ac deteriorem constituens.
paras.en: From the foregoing the Apostle infers that the faithful are bound to obey reason, not sensuality; the spirit, not the flesh. [[8:12|Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh to live according to the flesh|Ergo, o fratres, debitores sumus non carni, ut secundum carnem vivamus]]: that is, though we are in some way bound to the flesh, namely to supply it what it needs in food and clothing, yet we are not so bound to it as to yield to its concupiscences and live carnally. [[8:13|For if you live according to the flesh, you shall die|Si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini]], by the death of guilt in this world and by everlasting death in hell. [[8:13|but if by the Spirit|Si autem spiritu]], that is, by the grace of the Holy Ghost; or, by the spirit, that is, by the judgement of your reason, [[8:13|you mortify the deeds of the flesh|facta carnis mortificaveritis]], that is, the works, destroy them and cast them off as poisons: as is commanded in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 21:2|Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent|Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum]]; [[8:13|you shall live|vivetis]], the life of charity and grace in the Church militant, and the life of fruition and glory in the Church triumphant. Natural reason agrees with this teaching. For means must be ordered as the end requires. Since then the flesh is the instrument of the soul and is ordered to the spirit as to its end, it must be ruled as the soul or spirit requires: that it serve the soul, obey reason, and be occupied in those acts by which the spirit tends and returns to its Creator. But he who lives according to the flesh perverts this order, subjecting the mistress to the handmaid, putting the end after the means, and making himself viler and worse than the beasts.

paras.t: Quicumque enim Spiritu Dei aguntur, id est, a Spiritu Sancto reguntur, ejus instinctu ducuntur, ejus fervore impelluntur ad bona, hi sunt filii Dei, per gratiam adoptantem ac filialem amorem. Unde in Canonica Joannis scribitur : Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus. Quemadmodum autem Deus omnipotens movet ceteras creaturas ad proprias operationes, naturalemque finem, per quemdam universalem influxum seu generalem gubernationem (secundum quod Proclus auctor libri de Causis affirmat : Causa prima regit res omnes, præterquam quod commisceatur eis) ; sic rationalem creaturam movet ad finem supernaturalem per specialem gubernationem ac inspirationem, quæ providentia appellatur. Electos vero singulariter movet ac regit, providens eis non solum sufficienter, sed etiam efficaciter, de omnibus necessariis ad salutem, ita ut gratiam Dei suscipiant, ejusque inspirationi acquiescant. Idcirco dicuntur potius agi, quam regi vel moveri a Spiritu Sancto, ut magnitudo gratiæ insinuetur. Ad actum enim meritorium, non solum exigitur gratia habitualis, sed insuper necessaria est quædam actualis motio Spiritus Sancti voluntatem excitantis. Propter quod Propheta dicebat : Domine, omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis. — Porro, quum motio ista sive influxus, actio et instinctus Spiritus Sancti, sit penitus supernaturalis, indiget anima supernaturalibus quibusdam habitibus, per quos aptetur ac disponatur ad hujus motionis facilem susceptionem. Hi vero habitus, sunt septem dona Spiritus Sancti, quæ sunt dispositiones habituales ac supernaturales, a Deo immediate per creationem infusæ, quibus redditur anima facile mobilis a Spiritu Sancto in ordine ad supernaturalem finem, quæ est vita æterna. Hæc dona a virtutibus realiter distinguuntur, easque in dignitate excedunt, theologicis demptis virtutibus. Per hæc dona dirigitur anima a Spiritu Sancto, ita ut audiat eum sicut magistrum. Unde ait Psalmista : Spiritus tuus bonus deducet me in terram rectam. — Qui itaque sic aguntur Spiritu Dei, hi sunt filii Dei. Quicumque autem in gratia est, habet hæc dona secundum aliquem gradum, et agitur a Spiritu Sancto quantum requirit status salutis, videlicet ad observantiam præceptorum.
paras.en: [[8:14|For whosoever are led by the Spirit of God|Quicumque enim Spiritu Dei aguntur]], that is, are ruled by the Holy Ghost, led by His prompting, driven to good things by His fervour, [[8:14|they are the sons of God|hi sunt filii Dei]], by adopting grace and filial love. Hence it is written in the Canonical Epistle of John: [[1 John 3:1|Behold what manner of charity the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called and should be|Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus]]. Now as almighty God moves the other creatures to their proper operations and natural end by a certain universal influence or general government (as Proclus, the author of the book *On Causes*, affirms: The first cause rules all things without being mingled with them), so He moves the rational creature to its supernatural end by a special government and inspiration, which is called providence. And the elect He moves and rules singularly, providing them not only sufficiently but also efficaciously with all things necessary to salvation, so that they receive God's grace and yield to His inspiration. Therefore they are said rather to be *driven* [Latin *agi*, rendered “led” in the Douay] than ruled or moved by the Holy Ghost, to suggest the greatness of grace. For a meritorious act requires not only habitual grace, but also a certain actual motion of the Holy Ghost stirring the will. Wherefore the Prophet said: [[Is 26:12|Lord, thou wilt give us peace: for thou hast wrought all our works for us|Domine … omnia … opera nostra operatus es nobis]]. — Further, since this motion or influence, action and prompting of the Holy Ghost is wholly supernatural, the soul needs certain supernatural habits by which it is fitted and disposed to receive this motion readily. These habits are the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]], which are habitual and supernatural dispositions infused by God immediately by creation, whereby the soul is made readily movable by the Holy Ghost towards its supernatural end, which is life everlasting. These gifts are really distinct from the virtues and excel them in dignity, the theological virtues excepted. By these gifts the soul is directed by the Holy Ghost, so that it hears Him as a master. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 142:10|Thy good spirit shall lead me into the right land|Spiritus tuus bonus deducet me in terram rectam]]. — Those, then, who are thus led by the Spirit of God are the sons of God. And whoever is in grace has these gifts in some degree, and is led by the Holy Ghost as far as the state of salvation requires, namely to the keeping of the commandments.

paras.t: Deinde ponitur ratio cur morituri simus, si secundum carnem vixerimus. Non enim accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, id est, jam tempore gratiæ, non est vobis datus spiritus quo serviatis Deo serviliter quasi invite, videlicet timore pœnarum, ut olim tempore legis, quæ comminatione pœnarum induxit homines ad serviendum ; sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum Dei, id est spiritum cujus gratia homines adoptantur in filios Dei, in quo clamamus ore vel corde : Abba (Pater). Duo sunt nomina, unum Hebraeum, alterum Latinum, significantia idem. Et est sensus : In hoc spiritu vocamus ex caritate, tanquam filii adoptivi, Deum Patrem fiducialiter atque affectuose, dicentes : Pater noster qui es in cœlis.
paras.en: Next is given the reason why we shall die if we live according to the flesh. [[8:15|For you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear|Non enim accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore]], that is, now in the time of grace there has not been given you a spirit by which you serve God servilely, as it were unwillingly, namely through fear of punishment, as formerly in the time of the law, which by threat of punishment brought men to serve[[Deut 28:15||]]; [[8:15|but you have received the spirit of adoption of sons|sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum]] of God, that is, the spirit by whose grace men are adopted as sons of God, [[8:15|whereby we cry|in quo clamamus]] with mouth or heart: [[8:15|Abba (Father)|Abba (Pater)]]. These are two names, one Hebrew, the other Latin, meaning the same. And the sense is: In this spirit we call upon God the Father out of charity, as adopted sons, confidently and lovingly, saying: [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven|Pater noster qui es in cœlis]].

paras.t: Glossa per spiritum servitutis, intelligit Spiritum Sanctum, a quo cordibus Judæorum incussus est timor pœnarum, quo serviliter servierunt. Nam et timor servilis, in quantum est timor, a Spiritu Sancto est. Sic enim retrahit a peccato et disponit ad gratiam. Quantum vero ad servilitatem suam, nec bonus est, neque a Spiritu Sancto. Dicitur ergo Spiritus Sanctus, spiritus servitutis, ratione sui effectus, quia facit servire. Quantum ad hoc, receperunt [eum] qui ejus dono gratis dato servierunt timore pœnarum. Per spiritum vero adoptionis, intelligit Glossa eumdem Spiritum Sanctum per gratiam adoptantem. Unde Augustinus : Cave, inquit, ne ex eo quod ait, Spiritum servitutis, et, Spiritum adoptionis, diversum intelligas spiritum, quum sit unus atque idem Spiritus, qui in Trinitate dicitur Spiritus Sanctus : quod etiam Apostolus ostendit, dicens, Iterum. Sed propter diversa opera dissimiliter nominatur. Huic dicto concordat quod de Spiritu subditur, Ipse enim Spiritus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro, quod sumus filii Dei : quod certum est dici de Spiritu Sancto, videturque dictum de eodem spiritu de quo nunc agitur.
paras.en: The Gloss understands by the spirit of bondage the Holy Ghost, by whom the fear of punishment was struck into the hearts of the Jews, through which they served servilely. For servile fear too, insofar as it is fear, is from the Holy Ghost; for thus it draws back from sin and disposes to grace. But as to its servility, it is neither good nor from the Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost, then, is called the spirit of bondage by reason of His effect, because He makes men serve. In this respect they received Him who, by His gift freely given [*gratis datum*, a grace given for others' good or without sanctifying], served through fear of punishment. By the spirit of adoption the Gloss understands the same Holy Ghost adopting through grace. Hence Augustine says: Beware lest, from his saying “the spirit of bondage” and “the spirit of adoption”, you understand a different spirit, since it is one and the same Spirit who in the Trinity is called the Holy Ghost: which the Apostle also shows by saying “again”. But because of different works He is named differently. With this agrees what is added of the Spirit: [[8:16|For the Spirit himself giveth testimony to our spirit that we are the sons of God|Ipse enim Spiritus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro, quod sumus filii Dei]]: which is certainly said of the Holy Ghost, and seems said of the same spirit now treated.

paras.t: Quidam vero per spiritum intelligunt donum Spiritus Sancti : ut spiritus adoptionis dicatur donum filialis timoris, qui nos efficit filios Dei; spiritus vero servitutis intelligatur donum timoris servilis, videlicet ipse timor servilis. Hæc enim, secundum Augustinum, est brevis differentia legis et Evangelii : timor et amor. Lex vetus appellata est lex timoris, quoniam comminatione pœnarum induxit ad bonum, nec præstitit gratiam obediendi per caritatem. Porro lex evangelica, est lex amoris : agit enim, gratiam conferendo, servire Deo amore justitiæ. Non est autem sic intelligendum, quin multi in veteri Testamento acceperunt spiritum adoptionis filiorum Dei. Omnes enim electi habuerunt hunc spiritum, sed non ex lege, neque per legem, magis autem ex Deo per fidem qua crediderunt in Christum venturum, ad cujus gratiam confugerunt, legis insufficientiam cognoscentes, propriamque infirmitatem pensantes.
paras.en: Some, however, understand by spirit a gift of the Holy Ghost: so that the spirit of adoption is the gift of filial fear, which makes us sons of God, and the spirit of bondage is the gift of servile fear, namely servile fear itself. For this, according to Augustine, is the brief difference between the Law and the Gospel: fear and love. The old law was called the law of fear because it led to good by threat of punishment and did not give the grace of obeying through charity. But the Gospel law is the law of love: for by conferring grace it makes men serve God out of love of justice. Yet this is not to be understood as though many in the Old Testament did not receive the spirit of adoption of the sons of God. For all the elect had this spirit, but not from the law nor through the law, but rather from God, through the faith by which they believed in Christ to come, to whose grace they fled, knowing the insufficiency of the law and weighing their own weakness.

paras.t: Videtur quoque per spiritum hoc loco posse intelligi spiritus rationalis creatus, videlicet anima nostra. Quamvis autem quilibet nostrum acceperit hunc spiritum suum, quando creata corporique infusa est anima sua, dicimur tamen spiritum istum recipere vel amittere, quando aliqua nova dispositio ei confertur vel aufertur, quemadmodum aliquis dicitur concipere spiritum devotum, vel perdere animam ferventem. Juxta quem sensum Dominus ait : Auferam cor lapideum de carne vestra, et dabo vobis cor carneum. Qui ergo sub lege servierunt timore, accepisse dicuntur spiritum servitutis, id est animam servientem in timore. Qui vero sub gratia serviunt caritate, accipiunt spiritum adoptionis, id est animam habentem gratiam adoptionis : in quo spiritu clamant corde devoto, Abba (Pater). Huic vero consonat quod alibi ait Apostolus : Non dedit nobis Deus spiritum timoris, sed virtutis et dilectionis.
paras.en: It seems too that by spirit in this place may be understood the created rational spirit, namely our soul. Although each of us received this his spirit when his soul was created and infused into the body, we are yet said to receive or lose this spirit when some new disposition is conferred on it or taken from it, as one is said to conceive a devout spirit or to lose a fervent soul. In which sense the Lord says: [[Ezech 36:26|I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a heart of flesh|Auferam cor lapideum de carne vestra, et dabo vobis cor carneum]]. Those, then, who under the law served in fear are said to have received the spirit of bondage, that is, a soul serving in fear. But those who under grace serve in charity receive the spirit of adoption, that is, a soul having the grace of adoption: in which spirit they cry with devout heart, Abba (Father). With this agrees what the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Tim 1:7|For God hath not given us the spirit of fear: but of power and of love|Non dedit nobis Deus spiritum timoris, sed virtutis et dilectionis]].

paras.t: Quod autem in Spiritu Sancto clamemus, Abba (Pater), et Deum vere Patrem vocemus, hinc constat : Ipse enim Spiritus Sanctus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro, id est, testificatur animæ nostræ, eamque recognoscere facit per inspirationem internam, vel revelationem apertam, quod sumus filii Dei adoptivi, stando in caritate et gratia.
paras.en: That we cry in the Holy Ghost, Abba (Father), and truly call God Father, is clear from this: [[8:16|For the Spirit himself giveth testimony to our spirit|Ipse enim Spiritus Sanctus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro]] (the Holy Ghost), that is, testifies to our soul and makes it recognize, by inward inspiration or open revelation, [[8:16|that we are the sons of God|quod sumus filii Dei]] by adoption, while we stand in charity and grace.

paras.t: Testificatio ista multis modis intelligi potest. Primo, per manifestam et claram revelationem Spiritus Sancti, sive fiat immediate ab ipso, sive per angelum : sicque agnoscit homo per certitudinem se esse in gratia et filiatione divina, sicut Paulus et ceteri Apostoli, imo et multi perfecti ita sciverunt se esse in gratia. Ad quos maxime pertinet quod alio loco dicit Apostolus : Nos non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis. Hoc modo agnovit Abraham se esse filium Dei, quum ei Dominus promisit quod decederet in senectute bona. Ezechias quoque certissime dixit : Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et in corde perfecto. Secundo, fit testificatio ista per quamdam bonæ fiduciæ consolatoriam infusionem : ut quum homo nimium anxiatur an placeat Deo, et subito sentit se consolari et quasi certificari. Sic autem omnes virtuosi et boni scire possunt se esse filios Dei, non quidem certo, sed conjecturaliter et probabiliter. Tertio, fit per propriæ conversationis et conscientiæ diligentem discussionem : ut quum homo non habet remorsum mortalis peccati, et cum debita diligentia custodit mandata, auditque verbum Dei libenter. Ista sunt probabilia signa filiationis divinæ, imo et prædestinationis, secundum quod ait Salvator : Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit; et Joannes in sua Canonica, Si cor nostrum non reprehenderit nos, fiduciam habemus ad Deum ; et rursus, Qui servat verbum Christi, vere in hoc caritas Dei perfecta est. — Denique, sicut vita naturæ cognoscitur ex vitalibus actibus ac naturalibus motibus animæ, sic vita gratiæ ex bonis operibus, seu mandatorum custodia comprobatur, quia ut Gregorius ait, Exhibitio operis, probatio est caritatis. Quum ergo Spiritus Sanctus facit nos bene agere, atque in Dei obsequio promptos et agiles esse, tunc utique testimonium perhibet spiritui nostro, quod filii Dei simus.
paras.en: This testimony can be understood in many ways. First, by a manifest and clear revelation of the Holy Ghost, whether made immediately by Him or through an angel: and so a man knows with certainty that he is in grace and divine sonship, as Paul and the other Apostles, and indeed many perfect souls, thus knew themselves to be in grace. To these chiefly belongs what the Apostle says in another place: [[1 Cor 2:12|Now, we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God: that we may know the things that are given us from God|Nos non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis]]. In this way Abraham knew himself to be a son of God, when the Lord promised him that he should die in a good old age[[Gen 15:15||]]. Ezechias also most certainly said: [[4 Kings 20:3|remember how I have walked before thee in truth, and with a perfect heart|Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et in corde perfecto]]. Secondly, this testimony is given by a consoling infusion of good confidence: as when a man is greatly anxious whether he pleases God, and suddenly feels himself consoled and as it were assured. In this way all virtuous and good men can know that they are sons of God, not indeed with certainty, but by conjecture and probably. Thirdly, it is given through diligent examination of one's own conduct and conscience: as when a man has no remorse of mortal sin, keeps the commandments with due diligence, and gladly hears the word of God. These are probable signs of divine sonship, and even of predestination, as the Saviour says: [[John 8:47|He that is of God heareth the words of God|Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit]]; and John in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 3:21|if our heart do not reprehend us, we have confidence towards God|Si cor nostrum non reprehenderit nos, fiduciam habemus ad Deum]]; and again: [[1 John 2:5|But he that keepeth his word, in him in very deed the charity of God is perfected|Qui servat verbum Christi, vere in hoc caritas Dei perfecta est]]. — Lastly, as the life of nature is known from the vital acts and natural movements of the soul, so the life of grace is proved by good works, or the keeping of the commandments; for, as Gregory says, the showing of the work is the proof of love. When therefore the Holy Ghost makes us act well and be prompt and nimble in God's service, then indeed He bears witness to our spirit that we are sons of God.

paras.t: Huic ergo dicto Apostoli non repugnat quod scriptum est : Sunt justi atque sapientes, et opera eorum in manu Dei sunt ; et tamen nescit homo utrum amore an odio dignus sit, sed omnia in futurum servantur incerta. Et quod ait beatus Job : Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum, et si recesserit a me, non intelligam ; itemque, Si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea. Hæc enim atque similia ideo asseruntur, quia de lege communi et humano processu seu via, non potest homo agnoscere per certitudinem se esse filium Dei per gratiæ adoptionem. Postremo, melius atque facilius potest quis scire se esse in gratia et esse filium Dei secundum præsentem justitiam, quam esse prædestinatum, vel in gratia permansurum. Unde hoc certo agnosci non potest, nisi per revelationem divinam.
paras.en: This saying of the Apostle, then, is not contradicted by what is written: [[Eccles 9:1|there are just men and wise men, and their works are in the hand of God|Sunt justi atque sapientes, et opera eorum in manu Dei sunt]]: and yet [[Eccles 9:1|man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred|nescit homo utrum amore an odio dignus sit]], [[Eccles 9:2|But all things are kept uncertain|sed omnia in futurum servantur incerta]]. Nor by what blessed Job says: [[Job 9:11|If he come to me, I shall not see him: if he depart, I shall not understand|Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum, et si recesserit a me, non intelligam]]; and likewise: [[Job 9:21|Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of|Si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea]]. For these and like things are asserted because by the common law and the human course or way a man cannot know with certainty that he is a son of God by the adoption of grace. Finally, one can know better and more easily that he is in grace and a son of God according to present justice than that he is predestined or will persevere in grace. This latter cannot be known with certainty except by divine revelation.

paras.t: Si autem filii Dei jam sumus per gratiam adoptantem, et heredes erimus in patria per gloriam beatificantem. Filiis enim adoptivis debetur aliqua pars hereditatis paternæ. Erimus autem heredes quidem, non cujuscumque, sed Dei, æternaliter possidendo bona Domini in terra viventium, quæ oculus non vidit nec auris audivit. Maxime tamen ista Beatorum hereditas est ipsa Divinitas, quæ est objectalis beatitudo indivisibilis in se : quæ tota habetur a singulis, a nullo autem totaliter, et ita dividitur secundum quod diversimode participatur : quæ diversitas est ex parte recipientium, quorum unus alio clarius conspicit Deum. De hac hereditate fertur in Psalmo : Dominus pars hereditatis meæ ; et, Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua. Per Isaiam quoque Dominus loquitur : Sustollam te super altitudinem terræ, et cibabo te hereditate patris tui Jacob. Ceteræ hereditates terminantur in morte. Hæc autem a morte sumit exordium, juxta illud : Quum dederit dilectis suis somnum, ecce hereditas Domini. Coheredes autem Christi, id est, beatitudinis Christi consortes atque participes erimus. Ipse est enim principalis heres, et nos simul cum ipso divinam beatitudinem consequemur. Quo autem merito, subditur : si tamen compatimur, id est, Christi passionibus configuremur, bajulando crucem nostram, et sequendo vestigia ejus : ad hunc finem, ut et simul glorificemur, id est, gloriosi efficiamur cum Christo glorificato, quemadmodum ipse profitetur : Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam.
paras.en: [[8:17|And if sons|Si autem filii]] of God we now are by adopting grace, [[8:17|heirs also|et hæredes]] we shall be in the fatherland by beatifying glory. For to adopted sons some part of the father's inheritance is due. And we shall be [[8:17|heirs indeed of God|hæredes, quidem Dei]], not of anyone at all, but of God, possessing eternally the good things of the Lord in the land of the living[[Ps 26:13||]], which [[1 Cor 2:9|Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|oculus non vidit nec auris audivit]]. But above all this inheritance of the Blessed is the Godhead itself, which is the objective beatitude, indivisible in itself: which is had wholly by each, but by none totally [that is, each possesses the whole God, but none comprehends Him fully], and so is divided according as it is shared in diverse ways; which diversity is on the part of the receivers, one of whom sees God more clearly than another. Of this inheritance it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 15:5|The Lord is the portion of my inheritance|Dominus pars hereditatis meæ]]; and: [[Ps 16:15|I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear|Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua]]. Through Isaias also the Lord says: [[Is 58:14|I will lift thee up above the high places of the earth, and will feed thee with the inheritance of Jacob thy father|Sustollam te super altitudinem terræ, et cibabo te hereditate patris tui Jacob]] [the margin gives Is. lviii, 14]. Other inheritances end at death; but this one takes its beginning from death, according to that: [[Ps 126:2|When he shall give sleep|Quum dederit dilectis suis somnum]], [[Ps 126:3|Behold the inheritance of the Lord|ecce hereditas Domini]]. [[8:17|and joint heirs with Christ|cohæredes autem Christi]], that is, we shall be sharers and partakers of Christ's beatitude. For He is the principal heir, and we together with Him shall attain the divine beatitude. And by what merit is added: [[8:17|if we suffer with him|si tamen compatimur]], that is, if we are conformed to the sufferings of Christ, carrying our cross[[Matt 16:24||]][[Luke 14:27||]] and following in His footsteps: to this end, [[8:17|that we may be also glorified with him|ut et conglorificemur]] [Denis divides it, *simul glorificemur*], that is, be made glorious with Christ glorified, as He Himself declares: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam]].

8.title: PROSECUTIO EXPOSITIONIS HUJUS CAPITULI OCTAVI, AB EO LOCO QUO DICITUR : EXISTIMO ENIM QUOD NON SUNT CONDIGNÆ, ETC.
8.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this eighth chapter, from the place where it is said: For I reckon that the sufferings are not worthy, etc.

paras.t: HORTATUR nos insuper sanctus Apostolus, ut Christo compatiamur, quatenus conglorificemur, eo quod præmium incomparabiliter majus sit merito. Existimo enim, id est, agnosco ego, qui de talibus veraciter judico. Dicit autem, Existimo, non quasi incertus aut dubitans, sed sobrium modum loquendi servans, ac edocens ne immoderati simus in asserendo. Quod non sunt condignæ, id est æquales, sufficientes ac proportionatæ, secundum rigorem justitiæ, passiones, id est persecutiones, tentationes, labores, hujus temporis, id est, quas in hoc brevi vitæ hujus curriculo sustinemus, ad futuram gloriam, scilicet vitam æternam promerendam, quæ revelabitur in nobis, id est, clare et coram omnibus nobis prædestinatis præstabitur. Unde Salvator : Quum feceritis, ait, omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite : Servi inutiles sumus. Hæc enim gloria, est beatifica visio divinæ essentiæ, plena mentis in Deo lætitia, status omnium bonorum aggregatione perfectus, consummata animæ et corporis glorificatio sempiterna : ad quam promerendam, temporales passiones condignæ non sunt. — Sed videtur contrarium, quia secundum doctores, homo in caritate stans, meretur de condigno vitam æternam. Et respondendum, quod passiones seu opera caritatis considerantur dupliciter : Primo, secundum quod procedunt a libero arbitrio, vel acceptantur ab eo : sicque non merentur vitam æternam de condigno, etiam habitu caritatis adjuncto. Secundo, prout Spiritus Sanctus liberum arbitrium movens, est hujus processionis vel acceptationis principium : et ita est meritum de condigno, eo quod principium meriti ejusdem rationis exsistat cum præmio. Apostolus vero loquitur de passionibus primo modo.
paras.en: The holy Apostle further exhorts us to suffer with Christ, so that we may be glorified with Him, because the reward is incomparably greater than the merit. [[8:18|For I reckon|Existimo enim]], that is, I acknowledge, I who judge truly of such things. He says *I reckon*, not as one uncertain or doubting, but keeping a sober manner of speech, and teaching us not to be immoderate in asserting. [[8:18|are not worthy to be compared|Quod non sunt condignæ]], that is, equal, sufficient and proportioned according to the rigour of justice, [[8:18|the sufferings|passiones]], that is, persecutions, temptations, labours, [[8:18|of this time|hujus temporis]], that is, which we bear in this brief course of this life, [[8:18|with the glory to come|ad futuram gloriam]], namely for meriting eternal life, [[8:18|that shall be revealed in us|quæ revelabitur in nobis]], that is, which shall be bestowed clearly and openly upon all of us who are predestined. Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 17:10|when you shall have done all these things that are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable servants|feceritis, ait, omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite : Servi inutiles sumus]]. For this glory is the beatific vision of the divine essence, the full joy of the mind in God, a state made perfect by the gathering of all goods, the consummate and everlasting glorification of soul and body: for meriting which temporal sufferings are not worthy. — But the contrary seems true, since according to the doctors a man standing in charity merits eternal life *de condigno* [that is, by a merit strictly proportioned to the reward, as distinct from merit *de congruo*, of fittingness]. The answer is that sufferings or works of charity are considered in two ways. First, as they proceed from free will or are accepted by it: and so they do not merit eternal life *de condigno*, even with the habit of charity added. Second, inasmuch as the Holy Ghost, moving free will, is the principle of this proceeding or accepting: and thus there is merit *de condigno*, because the principle of the merit is of the same order as the reward. The Apostle speaks of sufferings in the first way.

paras.t: Quod autem gloria ista nobis præstanda sit, probat. Nam exspectatio creaturæ, id est creatura exspectans, videlicet homo viator. Dicitur enim homo omnis creatura, juxta illud, Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ : primo, propter communionem, quia cum omni genere creaturarum in aliquo convenit; secundo, propter excellentiam, quoniam omnia corporalia propter ipsum creata sunt. Revelationem filiorum Dei exspectat, id est, manifestationem beatitudinis electorum in patria, scilicet sui ipsius felicitatem et glorificationem, cum ingenti desiderio præstolatur, dicens quotidie : Quemadmodum desiderat cervus ad fontes aquarum, ita desiderat anima mea ad te, Deus. Nunc quippe filii Dei sumus, et nondum apparuit quid erimus. Scimus quoniam quum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est. Nunc ergo exspectamus hanc apparitionem, quatenus mente et corpore glorificati, declaremur seu agnoscamur esse filii Dei per similitudinem gloriæ.
paras.en: That this glory is to be bestowed on us he proves. [[8:19|For the expectation of the creature|Nam exspectatio creaturæ]], that is, the creature that waits, namely man the wayfarer. For man is called every creature, according to that saying, [[Mark 16:15|preach the gospel to every creature|Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]: first, by reason of communion, because he agrees in something with every kind of creature; second, by reason of excellence, since all bodily things were created for his sake[[Gen 1:26||]]. [[8:19|waiteth for the revelation of the sons of God|Revelationem filiorum Dei exspectat]], that is, it awaits with immense desire the manifestation of the beatitude of the elect in the fatherland, namely its own happiness and glorification, saying daily: [[Ps 41:2|As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; so my soul panteth after thee, O God|Quemadmodum desiderat cervus ad fontes aquarum, ita desiderat anima mea ad te, Deus]]. For [[1 John 3:2|we are now the sons of God: and it hath not yet appeared what we shall be. We know that when he shall appear we shall be like to him: because we shall see him as he is|Nunc quippe filii Dei sumus, et nondum apparuit quid erimus. Scimus quoniam quum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est]]. Now therefore we await this appearing, so that, glorified in mind and body, we may be declared or acknowledged to be sons of God by the likeness of glory.

paras.t: Vanitati enim, id est instabilitati, mortalitati, multisque pœnis, creatura subjecta est, id est homo, quemadmodum ait Scriptura : Verumtamen universa vanitas, omnis homo vivens; non volens, id est non sponte, quia invitus hæc patitur; vel, Non volens, id est propter originale peccatum, quod non est nostra voluntate commissum, cujus pœnas cogimur tolerare ; sed propter eum qui subjecit eam in spe, id est, propter divinam justitiam subjectus est homo vanitati huic, clementer tamen, quia in spe liberationis futuræ. Quia et ipsa creatura, videlicet homo, liberabitur, in futura resurrectione, a servitute corruptionis, id est corruptione ista servili et corporali, vel magis proprie a servitute corruptionis, id est sollicitudinibus vitæ præsentis, videlicet a cura quærendi vestitum et victum, ac alia quibus hæc corruptibilis vita sustentatur, eique servitur. Liberabitur autem, pertingendo in libertatem gloriæ, id est in dominium et securitatem felicitatis, vel in gloriosam libertatem filiorum Dei, id est electorum seu Beatorum in patria, qui Deo perfecte assimilantur, et plena dilectione incessabiliter conjunguntur. Hæc autem consequenter declarat Apostolus.
paras.en: [[8:20|For the creature was made subject to vanity|Vanitati enim creatura subjecta est]]: *vanity*, that is, instability, mortality and many pains; *the creature*, that is, man, as Scripture says: [[Ps 38:6|all things are vanity: every man living|universa vanitas, omnis homo vivens]]; [[8:20|not willingly|non volens]], that is, not of its own accord, because it suffers these things unwillingly; or, *not willingly*, that is, on account of original sin, which was not committed by our own will, and whose penalties we are forced to bear; [[8:20|but by reason of him that made it subject, in hope|sed propter eum qui subjecit eam in spe]], that is, on account of divine justice man was made subject to this vanity, yet mercifully, because in hope of future deliverance. [[8:21|Because the creature also itself|Quia et ipsa creatura]], namely man, [[8:21|shall be delivered|liberabitur]] in the future resurrection [[8:21|from the servitude of corruption|a servitute corruptionis]], that is, from this servile and bodily corruption; or more properly, *from the servitude of corruption*, that is, from the cares of the present life, namely from the care of seeking clothing and food and the other things by which this corruptible life is sustained and served. And it shall be delivered by attaining [[8:21|into the liberty of the glory|in libertatem gloriæ]], that is, into the dominion and security of happiness, or into the glorious liberty [[8:21|of the children of God|filiorum Dei]], that is, of the elect or the Blessed in the fatherland, who are perfectly likened to God and unceasingly joined to Him in full love. These things the Apostle next explains.

paras.t: Scimus enim quod omnis creatura ingemiscit et parturit usque adhuc. Hoc duobus modis exponitur. Primo, de omni homine mortali : qui dicitur ingemiscere, suspirando ad patriam, et propter vitæ hujus angustias frequenter gemens et flens in hac valle lacrimarum; et parturire, id est cum dolore operari; usque adhuc, quia a principio mundi usque in præsens tempus ita fecit, et usque ad mortem finemque sæculi durabit gemitus iste et parturitio. Secundo exponitur generaliter de principalibus partibus hujus mundi sensibilis, scilicet elementis atque cœlestibus orbibus : quæ dicuntur ingemiscere et parturire metaphorice, sicut campus dicitur exsultare, et pratum ridere. Unde per gemitum eorum, intelligitur inclinatio vel appetitus eorum ad statum perfectiorem; per parturitionem autem, mutua generatio et corruptio quantum ad elementa, vel continua circumvolutio quantum ad cœlestia corpora. Ex quibus elicitur, quod secundum intentionem Apostoli, corpora cœlestia et elementa in fine sæculi, glorificatis electis judicioque peracto, innovabuntur, ita quod elementorum transmutatio et cœlestium corporum motus cessabunt, ampliori quoque lumine vestientur. Terra enim, ut fertur, in superficie lucida erit ut vitrum, aqua sicut crystallus, aer ut cœlum, ignis ut stellæ. Quantitas autem meliorationis cœlestium corporum nota est ei qui daturus est eam. Verumtamen de mensura decorationis solis et lunæ scriptum est : Erit lux lunæ sicut lux solis, et lux solis septempliciter sicut lux septem dierum. Tunc enim tanta erit lux lunæ, quanta nunc est lux solis; corpora quoque Beatorum septies clariora erunt, ut dicitur, sole. Hoc tamen secundum B. Thomam, nec ratione nec auctoritate probatur, quamvis certissime verum esse sciamus quod veritas ait : Fulgebunt justi sicut sol in regno Patris eorum.
paras.en: [[8:22|For we know that every creature groaneth and travaileth in pain, even till now|Scimus enim quod omnis creatura ingemiscit et parturit usque adhuc]]. This is expounded in two ways. First, of every mortal man: who is said to *groan* by sighing for the fatherland, and, because of the straits of this life, often groaning and weeping in this vale of tears; and to *travail*, that is, to work with pain; *even till now*, because from the beginning of the world until the present time he has done so, and this groaning and travail will last until death and the end of the world. Second, it is expounded generally of the principal parts of this sensible world, namely the elements and the heavenly spheres: which are said to groan and travail metaphorically, as a field is said to rejoice[[Ps 95:12||]] and a meadow to smile. So by their groaning is understood their inclination or appetite toward a more perfect state; by their travail, the mutual generation and corruption as regards the elements, or the continual revolution as regards the heavenly bodies. From which it is drawn that, according to the Apostle's intent, the heavenly bodies and the elements will be renewed at the end of the world, when the elect have been glorified and the judgement completed, so that the transmutation of the elements and the motion of the heavenly bodies will cease, and they will be clothed with greater light. For the earth, as is said, will be bright on its surface like glass, the water like crystal, the air like the sky, the fire like the stars. The amount of the bettering of the heavenly bodies is known to Him who is to give it. Yet of the measure of the adornment of sun and moon it is written: [[Is 30:26|the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days|Erit lux lunæ sicut lux solis, et lux solis septempliciter sicut lux septem dierum]]. For then the light of the moon will be as great as the light of the sun is now; and the bodies of the Blessed will be, as is said, seven times brighter than the sun. This, however, according to blessed Thomas, is proved neither by reason nor by authority, although we know most surely to be true what the Truth says: [[Matt 13:43|shall the just shine as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father|Fulgebunt justi sicut sol in regno Patris eorum]].

paras.t: Mihi præterea, semper salvo meliori judicio, videtur, quod sicut præsens locus quo dicitur, Scimus quod omnis creatura ingemiscit et parturit, exponitur de prædictis corporibus, sic superiora ab eo loco quo dictum est, Nam exspectatio creaturæ, de eisdem possint exponi : præsertim quum Apostolus, dicendo, Exspectatio creaturæ revelationem filiorum Dei exspectat, et ipsa creatura liberabitur a servitute corruptionis in libertatem gloriæ filiorum Dei, manifeste videatur distinguere inter creaturam, et filios Dei adoptionis de quibus prædixit, scilicet homines prædestinatos. Erit igitur sensus : Exspectatio creaturæ elementalis atque cœlestis, revelationem filiorum Dei, id est manifestam glorificationem hominum electorum, exspectat, secundum quod ex divina ordinatione inclinatur ad quamdam clarificationem, quam in fine sæculi sortitura est, filiis Dei revelatis. Non enim innovabuntur corpora elementaria atque cœlestia, nisi corporibus electorum glorificatis, vel simul cum illis. Merito autem exspectat : Vanitati enim, id est mutabilitati vel transmutationi, creatura prædicta subjecta est, non volens, id est non ex se ipsa aut propria inclinatione, loquendo de ea prout ordinata est a Deo ad statum perfectum parificandum statui electorum post finale judicium, sed propter eum qui subjecit eam in spe, id est, ex ordinatione divina subjecta est huic vanitati propter hominem, ut ei deserviat. Corpora enim cœlestia propter generationem inferiorum, maxime hominum, moventur, et in generationibus mixtorum elementa concurrunt. Hæc autem subjectio facta est in spe præmemoratæ meliorationis seu clarificationis elementalium atque cœlestium, quia et ipsa creatura cœlestis et elementalis liberabitur a servitute corruptionis, id est a statu suæ variabilitatis, et a transmutatione ac motu, quibus corruptibilibus istis deservit.
