[[9:8|That is to say|Id est]], […] [a line is missing from the transcription here: the lemma *not they that are the children of the flesh*] are the seed, that is, those begotten by natural power from Agar and Cetura[[Gen 16:15||]][[Gen 25:1||]], […] [the lemma *are the children of God* is missing] that is, chosen for the divine worship and sharers in the divine promise; [[9:8|but they that are the children of the promise|sed qui filii sunt promissionis]], that is, those born of Isaac according to the divine promise, namely those who shared the blessing of their fathers, as Jacob and his sons, [[9:8|are accounted for the seed|æstimantur in semine]], that is, are truly and worthily called sons of Abraham.

paras.t: Deinde ponit formam promissionis. Promissionis enim divinæ verbum hoc est: Secundum hoc tempus, id est eodem die, anno uno elapso, veniam ad te, o Abraham, et erit Saræ filius, id est, Sara conjux tua, me cooperante, filium tunc habebit. Verba sunt angeli loquentis ad Abraham in persona Dei. Sic ergo Isaac filius erat promissionis, quia divina virtute sterilem matrem visitante, conceptus est, sicut erat promissum. Allegat autem Apostolus has scripturas secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum, qua utebatur Ecclesia tempore Apostolorum usque Hieronymi tempora. Nostra vero translatio talis est: Revertens veniam ad te tempore isto, vita comite, etc.
paras.en: Then he gives the form of the promise. [[9:9|For this is the word of promise|Promissionis enim divinæ verbum hoc est]], the divine promise: [[9:9|According to this time|Secundum hoc tempus]], that is, on the same day, one year having passed, [[9:9|will I come|veniam]] to thee, O Abraham, [[9:9|And Sara shall have a son|et erit Saræ filius]], that is, Sara thy wife, with my help, shall then have a son. They are the words of the angel speaking to Abraham in the person of God. So Isaac was the son of the promise, since he was conceived by the divine power visiting his barren mother, as had been promised. The Apostle alleges these scriptures according to the translation of the Seventy, which the Church used from the time of the Apostles up to the time of Jerome. Our translation is as follows: [[Gen 18:10|I will return and come to thee at this time, life accompanying|Revertens veniam ad te tempore isto, vita comite]], etc.

paras.t: Non solum hæc illi, id est, divina promissio non tantum facta est Saræ; sed et Rebecca promissionem accepit, ex uno concubitu habens in utero filios duos, Isaac patriarchæ patris nostri, videlicet Jacob et Esau. Sicut enim Sara sterilis divina virtute concepit, et sicut unus filiorum Abrahæ electus est, altero ei postposito; sic unus filiorum Isaac est electus, altero derelicto. Scriptum est enim: Deprecatus est Isaac Dominum pro uxore sua, eo quod esset sterilis, et exaudivit eum, deditque conceptum Rebeccæ. Ex quibus patet quod filii non sint electi merito parentum.
paras.en: [[9:10|And not only she|Non solum hæc illi]], that is, the divine promise was not made to Sara only; [[9:10|But when Rebecca also|sed et Rebecca]] received a promise, [[9:10|had conceived at once|ex uno concubitu habens]], having two sons in her womb from one conception, [[9:10|of Isaac our father|Isaac patriarchæ patris nostri]], namely Jacob and Esau. For as Sara, being barren, conceived by divine power, and as one of Abraham's sons was chosen, the other being set aside for him, so one of Isaac's sons was chosen, the other being left. For it is written: [[Gen 25:21|And Isaac besought the Lord for his wife, because she was barren: and he heard him, and made Rebecca to conceive|Deprecatus est Isaac Dominum pro uxore sua, eo quod esset sterilis, et exaudivit eum, deditque conceptum Rebeccæ]]. From which it is plain that the sons are not chosen for the merit of their parents.

paras.t: Quod autem Rebecca promissionem habuit de speciali gratia unius filiorum suorum, ostendit Apostolus. Quum enim nondum nati fuissent Jacob et Esau, aut aliquid boni egissent aut mali. Ex quo patet error dicentium animas hominum ante mundum sensibilem conditas, et ante vitam præsentis sæculi bona aut mala egisse, propter quæ jam diversas gratias atque miserias consequuntur. Ut secundum electionem, id est liberam unius præ alio acceptationem seu divinam prædestinationem, propositum Dei, id est divina voluntas, præscientia vel decretum, maneret ratum, et impleretur secundum quod erat præordinatum; non ex operibus, id est non propter præcedentia merita sive demerita, sed ex vocante, id est ex gratia Dei vocantis, dictum est ei, puta Rebeccæ: Quia major serviet minori, id est, Esau primo egrediens, serviet Jacob. Hoc enim modo dictum est Rebeccæ: Duæ gentes in utero tuo sunt, populusque populum superabit, et major serviet minori. Verumtamen servitus ista non est impleta in Jacob et Esau; imo Esau potentior erat et ditior fratre suo Jacob; sed in posteris eorum impleta est. Tempore enim David descendentis a Jacob, facta est Idumæa descendens ab Esau, serviens regi David sub tributo. Per hæc quoque figuratum est, quod populus Judæorum prior fide, serviturus esset populo christiano posteriori vocatione. Judæi quippe capsarii nostri sunt, qui nobis libros apportant.
paras.en: That Rebecca had a promise of special grace for one of her sons the Apostle shows: [[9:11|For when the children were not yet born, nor had done any good or evil|Quum enim nondum nati fuissent Jacob et Esau, aut aliquid boni egissent aut mali]], Jacob and Esau. From which the error is plain of those who say that the souls of men were created before the sensible world and did good or evil before the life of this present age, for which they now obtain different graces and miseries. [[9:11|that the purpose of God according to election might stand|Ut secundum electionem propositum Dei maneret]], *according to election*, that is, the free acceptance of one rather than another, or the divine predestination; *the purpose of God*, that is, the divine will, foreknowledge or decree, *might stand* firm and be fulfilled according as it had been foreordained; [[9:12|Not of works|non ex operibus]], that is, not on account of preceding merits or demerits, [[9:12|but of him that calleth|sed ex vocante]], that is, of the grace of God who calls, [[9:12|it was said to her|dictum est ei]], namely to Rebecca: [[9:12|The elder shall serve the younger|Quia major serviet minori]], that is, Esau, who came out first, shall serve Jacob. For it was said to Rebecca in this way: [[Gen 25:23|Two nations are in thy womb|Duæ gentes in utero tuo sunt]] … [[Gen 25:23|and one people shall overcome the other, and the elder shall serve the younger|populusque populum superabit, et major serviet minori]]. Yet this servitude was not fulfilled in Jacob and Esau; nay, Esau was more powerful and richer than his brother Jacob[[Gen 33:9||]][[Gen 36:7||]]; but it was fulfilled in their descendants. For in the time of David, who descended from Jacob, Idumea, which descended from Esau, was made to serve King David under tribute[[2 Kings 8:14||]]. By these things too it was figured that the people of the Jews, first in faith, would serve the Christian people, later in calling. For the Jews are our book-bearers [*capsarii*, the slaves who carried their masters' books], who carry the books for us.

paras.t: Quoniam autem servitus ista seu reprobatio Esau et prælatio Jacob, signum erat electionis Jacob ad gloriam, et reprobationis Esau ad pœnam, ideo Apostolus dicta confirmat auctoritate prophetica. Sicut scriptum est: Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui, id est reprobavi. Diligere Dei, est velle alicui bonum conferre; odire vero, est gratiam juste subtrahere. Quoniam ergo Deus prædestinavit Jacob, ideo dilexit eum ab æterno, præparans ei gratiam in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro. Ex opposito autem dicitur Esau odisse.
paras.en: Since this servitude, or the rejection of Esau and the preferring of Jacob, was a sign of the election of Jacob to glory and of the rejection of Esau to punishment, the Apostle confirms what he has said by the authority of a prophet: [[9:13|As it is written: Jacob I have loved: but Esau I have hated|Sicut scriptum est: Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui]], that is, rejected. For God to love is to will to bestow good on someone; to hate is justly to withdraw grace. Since, then, God predestined Jacob, he loved him from eternity, preparing for him grace in the present and glory in the future. In the opposite way he is said to have hated Esau.

paras.t: Quid ergo dicemus? id est, si Deus sic unum diligit, et alium odit ac reprobat, quid ex hoc sequitur? Numquid iniquitas est apud Deum? Absit: quoniam rectus Dominus Deus noster, et non est iniquitas in eo. Origenes autem, qui dixit gratiam conferri vel subtrahi propter merita et demerita præcedentia in vita priori, sic arguit: Sicut justum est æqualibus dare æqualia, sic injustum est non inæqualibus dare inæqualia. Si ergo nulla merita præcesserunt, injustum esset uni potius quam alteri gratiam dari. Sed hæc ratio non convincit, quia in his quæ omnino gratis ac liberaliter dantur, injustitia locum non habet. Quod Salvator noster in Matthæo evidenter testatur, loquens de cultoribus vineæ, et murmuranti respondens: Amice, non facio tibi injuriam; tolle quod tuum est, et vade. An non licet mihi quod volo facere?
paras.en: [[9:14|What shall we say then?|Quid ergo dicemus?]] that is, if God thus loves one and hates and rejects another, what follows from this? [[9:14|Is there injustice with God? God forbid!|Numquid iniquitas est apud Deum? Absit]]: for [[Ps 91:16|the Lord our God is righteous, and there is no iniquity in him|rectus Dominus Deus noster, et non est iniquitas in eo]]. Origen, who said that grace is bestowed or withdrawn on account of merits and demerits that went before in an earlier life, argues thus: as it is just to give equal things to equals, so it is unjust to give unequal things to those who are not unequal. If, then, no merits went before, it would be unjust for grace to be given to one rather than another. But this reasoning does not convince, since in things given altogether freely and generously injustice has no place. Which our Saviour plainly testifies in Matthew, speaking of the labourers in the vineyard and answering the one who murmured: [[Matt 20:13|friend, I do thee no wrong|Amice, non facio tibi injuriam]]; [[Matt 20:14|Take what is thine, and go thy way|tolle quod tuum est, et vade]]. [[Matt 20:15|is it not lawful for me to do what I will?|An non licet mihi quod volo facere?]]

paras.t: Et hoc ostendit modo Apostolus auctoritate scripturæ quæ in Exodo continetur. Apostolus autem non verba, sed sensum allegat, nisi forte secundum aliam translationem. Moysi enim dicit Dominus loco prædicto: Miserebor, dando gratiam in vita præsenti, cujus miseror in æterna præscientia; et misericordiam præstabo, dando gloriam in futuro, cujus miserebor. Tanquam dicat: Dabo gratiam in præsenti ei quem ab æterno prædestinavi, et dabo gloriam in futuro cui nunc gratiam tribuo. Nostra translatio habet sic: Miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit.
paras.en: And the Apostle now shows this by the authority of the scripture contained in Exodus[[Ex 33:19||]]. The Apostle alleges not the words but the sense, unless perhaps according to another translation. [[9:15|For he saith to Moses|Moysi enim dicit]], the Lord, in the place mentioned: [[9:15|I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy|Miserebor, dando gratiam in vita præsenti, cujus miseror]], I will have mercy by giving grace in the present life on him on whom I have mercy in my eternal foreknowledge; [[9:15|And I will shew mercy to whom I will shew mercy|et misericordiam præstabo cujus miserebor]], by giving glory in the future. As if he said: I will give grace in the present to him whom I have predestined from eternity, and I will give glory in the future to him to whom I now grant grace. Our translation has it thus: [[Ex 33:19|I will have mercy on whom I will, and I will be merciful to whom it shall please me|Miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit]].

paras.t: Ex his infert Apostolus: Igitur non volentis neque currentis, sed miserentis est Dei: id est, non in potestate hominis volentis est, velle aliquid meritorie, nec est in potestate hominis currentis seu operantis, meritorie operari, sed utrumque dependet et oritur ex misericordia et gratia Dei, sicut alibi dicitur: Deus operatur in nobis velle et perficere pro bona voluntate. Cui consonat illud Jeremiæ: Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est ut ambulet, et dirigat gressus suos. Ideo ait Psalmista: Viam mandatorum tuorum cucurri quum dilatasti cor meum. Quum enim finis creationis nostræ sit supernaturalis, scilicet visio Dei per speciem, non possumus velle, cogitare, vel facere aliquid meritorium hujus finis ex puris naturalibus, sed incessabili gratia indigemus. Non ergo aliquid de nostris viribus præsumamus, sed semper cum profundissima humilitate ad divinæ pietatis gratiam properemus, dicentes singuli Deo: Trahe me post te. Nam et Christus ait: Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater meus traxerit eum.
paras.en: From this the Apostle infers: [[9:16|So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy|Igitur non volentis neque currentis, sed miserentis est Dei]]: that is, it is not in the power of a man who wills to will anything meritoriously, nor in the power of a man who runs, or works, to work meritoriously; but both depend on and spring from the mercy and grace of God, as is said elsewhere: [[Phil 2:13|it is God who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish, according to his good will|Deus operatur in nobis velle et perficere pro bona voluntate]] [Denis: "in us"]. With which agrees that word of Jeremias: [[Jer 10:23|I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his: neither is it in a man to walk, and to direct his steps|Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est ut ambulet, et dirigat gressus suos]]. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:32|I have run the way of thy commandments, when thou didst enlarge my heart|Viam mandatorum tuorum cucurri quum dilatasti cor meum]] [the margin reference is not legible in the transcription]. For since the end of our creation is supernatural, namely the vision of God face to face, we cannot will, think or do anything meritorious of this end from our bare natural powers, but need unceasing grace. Let us not, then, presume anything of our own strength, but always hasten with the deepest humility to the grace of the divine mercy, each of us saying to God: [[Cant 1:3|Draw me|Trahe me]] after thee. For Christ too says: [[John 6:44|No man can come to me, except the Father, who hath sent me, draw him|Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater meus traxerit eum]] [Denis: "except my Father draw him"].

paras.t: Dicit enim Scriptura Pharaoni: id est, merito dixi Deum misereri cui vult, nec esse hominis velle aut operari meritorie, Dicit enim Scriptura, id est Deus in Scriptura, Pharaoni: Quia in hoc ipsum excitavi te, id est, ad hoc vel idcirco feci et posui te, et de somno peccati quo eras sopitus, suscitavi te, non ad gratiam, sed ad malitiæ tuæ majorem ostensionem, ut ostendam in te virtutem, id est potentiam meam, percutiendo Ægyptum diversis plagis, teque ad ultimum submergendo in mari Rubro, et ut annuntietur nomen meum in universa terra, id est, fama majestatis meæ divulgetur ubique, et omnes agnoscant potentiam meam, auditis mirabilibus quæ feci in te. Dicitur autem Deus Pharaonem excitasse seu posuisse ut virtutem suam in ipso ostenderet, et nomen suum hominibus revelaret, plagando et ante plagarum illationem indurando Pharaonem, consecutive: quia tam potens ac bonus est Deus, ut non permitteret esse malos, nisi vellet et posset ex hoc elicere bona. Quamvis ergo agnovit Pharaonem sic obstinandum et periturum, fecit tamen et posuit eum, quia ex ejus obstinatione elicere potuit et voluit, per modum sequelæ, divinæ virtutis atque justitiæ ostensionem, divinique nominis propalationem. Quod autem sit iste sensus litteræ allegatæ, constat ex conclusione Apostoli, inferentis:
paras.en: [[9:17|For the scripture saith to Pharao|Dicit enim Scriptura Pharaoni]]: that is, rightly did I say that God has mercy on whom he will, and that it is not of man to will or to work meritoriously; *for the scripture*, that is, God in the Scripture, *saith to Pharao*: [[9:17|To this purpose have I raised thee|Quia in hoc ipsum excitavi te]][[Ex 9:16||]], that is, for this, or therefore, have I made and set thee, and roused thee from the sleep of sin in which thou wast sunk, not to grace, but to the fuller showing of thy malice, [[9:17|that I may shew my power in thee|ut ostendam in te virtutem meam]], that is, my might, by striking Egypt with various plagues[[Ex 7:1||]], and at last drowning thee in the Red Sea[[Ex 14:1||]], [[9:17|and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth|et ut annuntietur nomen meum in universa terra]], that is, that the fame of my majesty may be spread everywhere, and all may know my power, having heard the wonders I have done on thee. God is said to have raised or set Pharao that he might show his power in him and reveal his name to men, by striking Pharao with plagues and hardening him before the plagues were brought on, consecutively: because God is so powerful and good that he would not permit the wicked to exist unless he willed and was able to draw good from it. So although he knew that Pharao would be so obstinate and would perish, he still made and set him, since from his obstinacy he could and would draw, by way of consequence, the showing of the divine power and justice and the spreading abroad of the divine name. That this is the sense of the text alleged is clear from the Apostle's conclusion, who infers:

paras.t: Ergo cui vult miseretur, per gratiam deducendo ad gloriam. Hoc convenit Deo per se, ita ut prædestinatio ejus sit causa gratiæ et gloriæ. Et quem vult indurat, non influendo malitiam, sed non conferendo subsidium. Hoc convenit Deo per accidens, scilicet quia non removet prohibens. Sicut nauta per suam absentiam est causa submersionis navigantium; et sol per suam elongationem est causa congelationis, non impertiendo frigiditatem, sed non influendo calorem: sic Deus indurat, non adhibendo gratiam cordis duritiam mollificantem. Porro, reprobatio divina non est causa culpæ, sed pœnæ propter culpam. Sumendo ergo reprobationem divinam pro ordinatione alicujus ad pœnam, sic secundum ordinem rationis, præscientia peccatorum reprobationem præcedit, quoniam Deus neminem ordinat ad pœnam nisi quia agnoscit et præscit ejus malitiam.
paras.en: [[9:18|Therefore he hath mercy on whom he will|Ergo cui vult miseretur]], leading him through grace to glory. This belongs to God of himself, so that his predestination is the cause of grace and glory. [[9:18|And whom he will, he hardeneth|Et quem vult indurat]], not by pouring in malice, but by not bestowing help. This belongs to God by accident, namely because he does not remove what hinders. As a sailor by his absence is the cause of the drowning of those on board, and the sun by its withdrawal is the cause of freezing, not by imparting cold but by not pouring in heat: so God hardens by not applying the grace that softens hardness of heart. Further, the divine rejection is not the cause of guilt, but of punishment on account of guilt. Taking the divine rejection, then, for the ordering of someone to punishment, in the order of reason the foreknowledge of sins goes before rejection, since God orders no one to punishment except because he knows and foreknows his malice.

paras.t: Sed quia prædicta miranda sunt, et multis errandi occasionem ministrant, ideo movet Apostolus, quod noverat a carnalibus esse movendum. Dicis itaque mihi: id est, si Deus quem vult indurat, et cui vult miseretur, videtur quod sicut vocatio justi, ita induratio reprobi ex divina voluntate dependeat: ut sicut non est ex meritis quod Deus miseretur, ita non erit ex meritis quod reprobat; sicque imputabitur Deo quod unus sit bonus, et alius malus. Ideo subditur: Quid adhuc quæritur? id est, quum ista ita se habeant, cur ultra inquiritur cur iste sit bonus, et iste malus? vel, quid ab aliquo requiritur ut bene operetur? vel, cur Deus aut alius quisquam conqueritur de hoc quod quidam impie vivunt? voluntati enim ejus quis resistit? id est, quum nullus valeat divinæ resistere voluntati. Ista objectio fortis esset, si Deus esset directa et effectiva causa indurationis, sicut est directa et effectiva causa justificationis. Hoc autem ita non est, sicut jam patuit.
paras.en: But since what has been said is to be wondered at, and gives many an occasion of error, the Apostle raises the question he knew carnal men would raise. [[9:19|Thou wilt say therefore to me|Dicis itaque mihi]]: that is, if God hardens whom he will and has mercy on whom he will, it seems that, as the calling of the just man, so the hardening of the reprobate depends on the divine will: so that, as it is not from merits that God has mercy, so it will not be from merits that he rejects; and so it will be imputed to God that one man is good and another evil. Therefore there follows: [[9:19|Why doth he then find fault?|Quid adhuc quæritur?]] [Latin: "why is it still asked?"] that is, since these things are so, why is it further asked why this man is good and that one evil? or, why is anything required of anyone, that he should work well? or, why does God or anyone else complain that some live wickedly? [[9:19|For who resisteth his will?|voluntati enim ejus quis resistit?]] that is, since no one can resist the divine will[[Esth 13:9||]]. This objection would be strong if God were the direct and effective cause of hardening as he is the direct and effective cause of justification. But this is not so, as has already appeared.

paras.t: Apostolus demum respondet ad hoc, primo redarguens temeritatem eorum qui profunda Dei scrutari præsumunt. O homo mortalis, in ordine intellectualium substantiarum novissimus, qui nec te ipsum, nec inferiora te comprehendere potes, tu quis es qui respondeas Deo, opera ejus impugnando, intelligendo, vel ejus sermonibus responsa præstando? Nullum horum facere potes. Scriptum est enim: Intellexi quod omnium operum Dei nullam possit homo invenire rationem. Et in libro Sapientiæ: Difficile æstimamus quæ in terra sunt, et quæ in prospectu sunt invenimus cum labore; quæ autem in cœlis sunt, quis investigabit? Hinc ait beatus Job: Quis ego sum ut respondeam Deo, et loquar verbis meis cum eo? Et rursus: Si voluerit homo cum Deo contendere, non poterit respondere unum pro mille. Numquid dicit figmentum, id est opus, ei qui se finxit, Quid me fecisti sic? id est, sicut figmentum non dicit figulo, cur sic fecerit se, quia nec se ipsum nec figulum comprehendit; sic homo non debet dicere incomprehensibili factori suo: Cur ita fecisti, unum eligendo, alium dimittendo, plus gratiæ conferendo seu etiam præparando isti, quam mihi? Hoc verbum Apostoli, sumptum videtur ex eo quod Isaias ait: Væ qui contradicit factori suo: numquid dicit lutum figulo, Quid facis?
paras.en: Lastly the Apostle answers this, first rebuking the rashness of those who presume to search the depths of God. [[9:20|O man|O homo]], mortal, the last in the order of intellectual substances, who canst comprehend neither thyself nor the things beneath thee, [[9:20|who art thou that repliest against God?|tu quis es qui respondeas Deo]] by attacking his works, by understanding them, or by giving answers to his words? Thou canst do none of these. For it is written: [[Eccles 8:17|I understood that man can find no reason of all those works of God|Intellexi quod omnium operum Dei nullam possit homo invenire rationem]]. And in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 9:16|And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth: and with labour do we find the things that are before us. But the things that are in heaven, who shall search out?|Difficile æstimamus quæ in terra sunt, et quæ in prospectu sunt invenimus cum labore; quæ autem in cœlis sunt, quis investigabit?]] Hence blessed Job says: [[Job 9:14|What am I then, that I should answer him, and have words with him?|Quis ego sum ut respondeam Deo, et loquar verbis meis cum eo?]] And again: [[Job 9:3|If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one for a thousand|Si voluerit homo cum Deo contendere, non poterit respondere unum pro mille]]. [[9:20|Shall the thing formed|Numquid dicit figmentum]], that is, the work, [[9:20|say to him that formed it: Why hast thou made me thus?|ei qui se finxit, Quid me fecisti sic?]] that is, as the thing formed does not say to the potter why he has made it so, since it comprehends neither itself nor the potter, so man ought not to say to his incomprehensible maker: why hast thou done thus, choosing one and leaving another, bestowing or even preparing more grace for this man than for me? This word of the Apostle seems to be taken from what Isaias says: [[Is 45:9|Woe to him that gainsayeth his maker|Væ qui contradicit factori suo]] … [[Is 45:9|shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it: What art thou making|numquid dicit lutum figulo, Quid facis?]]

paras.t: Consequenter ponit Apostolus generalem rationem, cur Deus quosdam prædestinavit, et quosdam præscivit, ostenditque propositum suum per simile. An non habet potestatem figulus luti, ex eadem massa, id est ex eodem luto, quod est suæ artis materia, facere aliud quidem vas in honorem, id est ad usus honestos, et in forma decora, ut collocetur in mensa, aliud vero in contumeliam? id est, sicut figulus hoc potest, sic utique Deus in natura humana potest quosdam producere ad salutem, quosdam ad damnationem. Unde per Jeremiam testatur: Numquid sicut figulus non potero vobis facere, domus Israel? Ecce sicut lutum in manu figuli, ita vos in manu mea. Non tamen iniquus est Deus, quoniam nulli aliquid debet. Sed quum Deus etiam multa bona impendat perversis et reprobis, sicut subjungitur, patet quod non solum sit non injustus, sed etiam pius.
paras.en: Next the Apostle gives the general reason why God has predestined some and foreknown others, and shows his meaning by a likeness. [[9:21|Or hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump|An non habet potestatem figulus luti, ex eadem massa]], that is, of the same clay, which is the matter of his craft, [[9:21|to make one vessel unto honour|facere aliud quidem vas in honorem]], that is, for honourable uses and in a comely shape, so as to be set on the table, [[9:21|and another unto dishonour?|aliud vero in contumeliam?]] that is, as the potter can do this, so surely God, in human nature, can bring forth some to salvation and some to damnation. Hence he testifies through Jeremias: [[Jer 18:6|Cannot I do with you, as this potter, O house of Israel, saith the Lord? behold as clay is in the hand of the potter, so are you in my hand|Numquid sicut figulus non potero vobis facere, domus Israel? Ecce sicut lutum in manu figuli, ita vos in manu mea]]. Yet God is not unjust[[Ps 91:16||]], since he owes nothing to anyone. And since God also bestows many goods on the perverse and the reprobate, as is added, it is plain that he is not only not unjust but also merciful.

paras.t: Quod si Deus volens ostendere iram suam, id est justam vindictam, et notam facere potentiam suam, id est justitiæ suæ rigorem et potestatem in reprobis in hac vita, vel postea, ut in eis reluceat divina justitia, sicut in prædestinatis resplendet divina clementia; sustinuit tamen in multa patientia, id est, longanimiter et multum benigne exspectavit pœnitentiam perversorum, qui sunt vasa iræ apta in interitum, id est digna morte æterna, quoniam habent in se vitia, propter quæ Deus offenditur, et iratum se monstrat pœnas infligendo. Et quia impiorum damnatio cedit ad gloriam electorum, Apostolus subdit: ut ostenderet divitias gloriæ suæ, id est opulentissimam bonitatem suam, et copiosissimam gratiam, descendentem in vasa misericordiæ, id est in homines misericorditer prædestinatos, quæ præparavit in gloriam, id est, præordinavit et condidit ad conquirendam beatitudinem sempiternam.
paras.en: [[9:22|What if God, willing to shew his wrath|Quod si Deus volens ostendere iram]], that is, his just vengeance, [[9:22|and to make his power known|et notam facere potentiam suam]], that is, the rigour and power of his justice in the reprobate, in this life or afterwards, so that the divine justice may shine out in them as the divine clemency shines in the predestined; [[9:22|endured with much patience|sustinuit tamen in multa patientia]], that is, waited long-sufferingly and most kindly for the repentance of the perverse, who are [[9:22|vessels of wrath, fitted for destruction|vasa iræ apta in interitum]], that is, deserving eternal death, since they have vices in them on account of which God is offended and shows himself angry by inflicting punishments. And since the damnation of the wicked turns to the glory of the elect, the Apostle adds: [[9:23|That he might shew the riches of his glory|ut ostenderet divitias gloriæ suæ]], that is, his most abundant goodness and most plentiful grace, coming down [[9:23|on the vessels of mercy|in vasa misericordiæ]], that is, on men mercifully predestined, [[9:23|which he hath prepared unto glory|quæ præparavit in gloriam]], that is, foreordained and created to win everlasting beatitude.

paras.t: In his verbis declarat Apostolus, quantum ab homine capi potest vel sciri expedit, quæ sit communis ratio prædestinationis et reprobationis divinæ. Quippe ut Salomon ait, Omnia propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus; et in Ecclesiaste, Fecit Deus opera sua ut timeatur. Ex quibus elucescit, quod Deus propter se ipsum finaliter omnia fecit, videlicet ut sua perfectio in creaturis appareat, sicque ex consideratione earum Deus glorificetur, ametur, ac timeatur. Ad perfectionem autem divinæ naturæ, præcipue pertinent misericordia et justitia. Opera autem misericordiæ faciunt Deum amabilem; opera vero justitiæ reddunt eum terribilem. Utraque tamen faciunt eum gloriosum et honorandum. Ut ergo divina perfectio reluceret in rebus sub ratione misericordiæ, prædestinavit Deus nonnullos, quibus sola pietate præparavit gratiam viæ et gloriam patriæ. Volens quoque relucere in creaturis suam justitiam, quosdam reliquit, quos dicitur reprobare; quod secundum Augustinum, est nolle misereri. Unde Salomon ait: Fecit Deus impium ad diem malum. Et alibi dicit Scriptura: In diem perditionis servatur impius, et ad diem furoris ducetur. Verumtamen, quoniam bonitas atque perfectio Dei excellentius repræsentatur ac splendet in electis quam reprobis, ideo prædestinati, specialiter facti dicuntur ad gloriam Dei, juxta illud Isaiæ: Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum. Omnia hæc breviter tangit Apostolus quum ait, quod Deus ostendere volens iram et potentiam suam, sustinuit vasa iræ ut ostenderet divitias gloriæ suæ in vasis misericordiæ, id est in prædestinatis, de quibus subjungitur:
paras.en: In these words the Apostle makes plain, as far as man can grasp or it is expedient to know, what is the common reason of the divine predestination and rejection. For as Solomon says: [[Prov 16:4|The Lord hath made all things for himself|Omnia propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus]]; and in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 3:14|God hath made that he may be feared|Fecit Deus opera sua ut timeatur]] [Denis: "God hath made his works that he may be feared"]. From which it shines out that God made all things for himself as their end, namely that his perfection might appear in creatures, and so from considering them God might be glorified, loved and feared. And to the perfection of the divine nature belong above all mercy and justice. The works of mercy make God lovable; the works of justice make him terrible. Yet both make him glorious and worthy of honour. So that the divine perfection might shine out in things under the aspect of mercy, God predestined some, for whom out of mercy alone he prepared the grace of the way and the glory of the fatherland. And willing that his justice should shine out in creatures, he left some, whom he is said to reject; which, according to Augustine, is to will not to have mercy. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 16:4|the wicked also for the evil day|impium ad diem malum]] [Denis: "God hath made the wicked for the evil day"]. And elsewhere the Scripture says: [[Job 21:30|the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath|In diem perditionis servatur impius, et ad diem furoris ducetur]]. Yet, since the goodness and perfection of God is represented and shines more excellently in the elect than in the reprobate, therefore the predestined are said to be made specially for the glory of God, according to that word of Isaias: [[Is 43:7|And every one that calleth upon my name, I have created him for my glory|Omnem qui invocat nomen meum, in gloriam meam creavi eum]]. The Apostle touches briefly on all this when he says that God, willing to show his wrath and power, endured the vessels of wrath that he might show the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, that is, on the predestined, of whom there follows:

paras.t: Quos et vocavit ad fidem et gratiam per prædicationem Apostolorum, non solum ex Judæis, sed etiam ex gentibus: ex utroque enim populo quidam ad Christum conversi sunt; sicut in Osee propheta dicit: Vocabo, id est nominabo, non plebem meam, id est populum gentilem, plebem meam. Nam ante conversionem suam erant non plebs mea secundum præsentem justitiam, quamvis secundum æternam prædestinationem fuerint semper plebs mea. Et non dilectam meam, id est eamdem plebem quam tempore suæ idololatriæ non dilexi, quantum ad culpam, vocabo dilectam meam, id est mihi dilectam, quum fidem et caritatem habuerint. Tunc enim amici erunt. Et non misericordiam consecutam, id est gentilitatem, quæ ante Christi adventum expers erat gratiæ Dei, vocabo misericordiam consecutam, quum gratiam Christi receperit. Hoc quod dicitur, Misericordiam consecutam, construendum est separatim, ut sit sensus, quod plebs gentilis quum fuerit conversa, vocabitur misericordiam consecuta. Et erit, id est, continget quod subditur, quod etiam jam dudum constat impletum: In loco, id est in terris gentilium, […] me per servos meos […] Non plebs mea estis vos, o gentiles, quamdiu idolis deservitis; ibi vocabuntur gentes istæ ad fidem conversæ, filii adoptivi Dei vivi. Quotquot enim receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri.
paras.en: [[9:24|whom also he hath called|Quos et vocavit]] to faith and grace through the preaching of the Apostles, [[9:24|not only of the Jews but also of the Gentiles|non solum ex Judæis, sed etiam ex gentibus]]: for from both peoples some were converted to Christ; [[9:25|As in Osee he saith|sicut in Osee propheta dicit]], the prophet: [[9:25|I will call|Vocabo]], that is, I will name, [[9:25|that which was not my people|non plebem meam]], that is, the Gentile people, [[9:25|my people|plebem meam]][[Osee 2:24||]][[1 Pet 2:10||]]. For before their conversion they were not my people according to present justice, though according to eternal predestination they were always my people. [[9:25|and her that was not beloved|Et non dilectam]], mine, that is, the same people whom I did not love, as to their guilt, in the time of their idolatry, I will call [[9:25|beloved|dilectam]], mine, that is, beloved by me, when they have faith and charity. For then they will be friends. [[9:25|and her that had not obtained mercy|Et non misericordiam consecutam]], that is, the Gentile world, which before Christ's coming had no share in the grace of God, I will call [[9:25|one that hath obtained mercy|misericordiam consecutam]], when it has received the grace of Christ. This phrase, *that hath obtained mercy*, is to be construed separately, so that the sense is that the Gentile people, when it has been converted, will be called one that has obtained mercy. [[9:26|And it shalt be|Et erit]], that is, there will come to pass what follows, which is plain to have been fulfilled long since: [[9:26|in the place|In loco]], that is, in the lands of the Gentiles, […] me through my servants […] [a line or two is missing from the transcription here, with the lemma *where it was said unto them*] *you are not my people*, O Gentiles, as long as you serve idols; [[9:26|there they shall be called the sons of the living God|ibi vocabuntur filii Dei vivi]][[Osee 1:10||]], these Gentiles converted to the faith, adopted sons of the living God. For [[John 1:12|as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God|Quotquot enim receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri]].

paras.t: Consequenter declarat Apostolus non omnes Judæos incredulos esse Domino Salvatori. Isaias autem clamat, id est, manifeste prophetat et dicit, pro Israel, id est de salvatione Judæorum: Si fuerit numerus filiorum Israel tanquam arena maris, id est, quamvis populus Israel præ multitudine innumerabilis fuerit, reliquiæ salvæ fient, id est, aliqui, numero pauci respectu aliorum, salvabuntur credendo in Christum: sicut in primitiva Ecclesia factum agnoscimus. Quomodo autem salvæ fient, adjecit: Verbum enim consummans et abbrevians in æquitate: hoc est, doctrina Christi, seu verbum Evangelii, est consummans, id est observantem ad perfectionem perducens, et præcepta legis consiliis suis perficiens; et abbrevians, id est brevi sermone perfectionem includens, innumerabiles legis cærimonias observantiasque excludens; in æquitate, id est in approbatione et observatione præceptorum moralium, quæ justa sunt atque servanda, quum sint de actibus virtutum; quia verbum breviatum, id est compendiosum, faciet Dominus Christus super terram. Hoc verbum breviatum quod Christus prædicavit in mundo, est caritatis præceptum, qua Deus proximusque diligitur. De quo verbo dicit in Evangelio: In hoc tota lex pendet et Prophetæ.
paras.en: Next the Apostle makes plain that not all the Jews are unbelieving toward the Lord the Saviour. [[9:27|And Isaias cried out concerning Israel|Isaias autem clamat pro Israel]], *cried out*, that is, prophesies and says plainly, *concerning Israel*, that is, of the salvation of the Jews: [[9:27|If the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea|Si fuerit numerus filiorum Israel tanquam arena maris]][[Is 10:22||]], that is, though the people of Israel be beyond counting for multitude, [[9:27|a remnant shall be saved|reliquiæ salvæ fient]], that is, some, few in number compared with the rest, will be saved by believing in Christ: as we know was done in the early Church. And how they will be saved he adds: [[9:28|For he shall finish his word and cut it short in justice|Verbum enim consummans et abbrevians in æquitate]] [the Latin reads "a word finishing and cutting short in equity"]: that is, the teaching of Christ, or the word of the Gospel, is *finishing*, that is, bringing him who keeps it to perfection, and perfecting the precepts of the law by its counsels; and *cutting short*, that is, enclosing perfection in a brief saying and shutting out the countless ceremonies and observances of the law; *in equity*, that is, in approving and keeping the moral precepts, which are just and to be kept, since they concern acts of the virtues; [[9:28|because a short word shall the Lord make upon the earth|quia verbum breviatum faciet Dominus super terram]], *short*, that is, compendious, the Lord Christ. This short word which Christ preached in the world is the precept of charity, by which God and neighbour are loved. Of which word he says in the Gospel: [[Matt 22:40|On these two commandments dependeth the whole law and the prophets|In hoc tota lex pendet et Prophetæ]] [Denis: "on this"].

paras.t: Sciendum vero, quod Isaias ubi præallegata verba inducit, loquitur de impugnatione filiorum Israel a rege Assyriorum, temporibus Ezechiæ regis Juda, vel Osee regis Israel, ut alii asserunt. Ideo quidam dicit prædicta verba Isaiæ ad litteram intelligenda esse de filiis Israel evadentibus manum regis Assyriorum. Sed hoc non videtur, quia Apostolus hoc loco apertissime ait, quod Isaias clamat pro filiis Israel qui salvantur per Christum, quemadmodum Osee propheta clamat pro gentibus ad fidem conversis. Præterea, quod adjungit Isaias, Verbum enim consummans et abbrevians, etc., est ratio verbi prædicti de salvatione reliquiarum Israel per Christum facta. Hieronymus autem, Augustinus, Ambrosius, et omnes pene doctores catholici, exponunt hoc ad litteram de verbo evangelicæ legis. Ergo salvatio illa non est intelligenda de temporali et corporali liberatione a rege Assyriorum, sed de salvatione spirituali atque æterna facta per Christum. Unde Hieronymus, Prophetarum studiosissimus explanator, exponendo præmemorata verba, dicit quod Isaias, descripta particulari, temporali ac figurativa liberatione Judæorum a rege Assyriorum, oculum mentis convertit ad salvationem universalem, spiritualem atque perfectam per Christum exhibitam. Et probat hoc S. Hieronymus auctoritate Apostoli, qui præsenti capitulo probat conversionem reliquiarum Israel prædicta auctoritate Isaiæ. Probatio autem per Scripturam, non valet nisi secundum sensum litteralem, ut Augustinus frequenter commemorat.
paras.en: It must be known that Isaias, where he brings in the words alleged, is speaking of the attack on the children of Israel by the king of the Assyrians, in the times of Ezechias king of Juda, or of Osee king of Israel, as others assert. Therefore a certain writer says that these words of Isaias are to be understood literally of the children of Israel escaping the hand of the king of the Assyrians. But this does not seem right, since the Apostle says most plainly in this place that Isaias cries out concerning the children of Israel who are saved through Christ, as the prophet Osee cries out concerning the Gentiles converted to the faith. Moreover, what Isaias adds, [[9:28|For he shall finish his word and cut it short|Verbum enim consummans et abbrevians]], etc., is the reason for the saying about the salvation of the remnant of Israel wrought through Christ. And Jerome, Augustine, Ambrose and almost all Catholic doctors explain this literally of the word of the law of the Gospel. That salvation, then, is not to be understood of a temporal and bodily deliverance from the king of the Assyrians, but of the spiritual and eternal salvation wrought through Christ. Hence Jerome, the most zealous explainer of the Prophets, expounding these words, says that Isaias, having described the particular, temporal and figurative deliverance of the Jews from the king of the Assyrians, turns the eye of his mind to the universal, spiritual and perfect salvation brought about through Christ. And St Jerome proves this by the authority of the Apostle, who in the present chapter proves the conversion of the remnant of Israel by this authority of Isaias. And proof from Scripture is valid only according to the literal sense, as Augustine often recalls.

paras.t: Et sicut prædixit Isaias in libro visionum suarum: Nisi Dominus Sabaoth, id est exercituum, vel virtutum, præsertim cœlestium: de quo angeli clamant: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus exercituum. Secundum Hieronymum, pro eo quod est Sabaoth, Septuaginta interpretes ponunt, Omnipotens. Quibus consonare videtur, quod Joannes in Apocalypsi verba Isaiæ inducens, sic ait: Requiem non habebant, dicentia: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus omnipotens. Itaque, Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis Judæis semen, id est reliquias in Christum credentes, videlicet sanctos Apostolos et ceteros ex Judaismo conversos, de quibus per Prophetam dicitur: Isti sunt semen cui benedixit Dominus; sicut Sodoma facti essemus, et sicut Gomorrha similes fuissemus, id est, penitus damnati essemus propter nostram incredulitatem, sicut perierunt habitatores Sodomæ et Gomorrhæ, cum aliis trium urbium habitatoribus, scilicet Adama, Seboim et Segor. Quidam exponit hæc verba Isaiæ ad litteram de Judæis non occisis a rege Assyriorum tempore Ezechiæ. Sed expositio talis repellitur eisdem rationibus quibus præcedens.
paras.en: [[9:29|And Isaias foretold|Et sicut prædixit Isaias]], in the book of his visions[[Is 1:9||]]: [[9:29|Unless the Lord of Sabbath|Nisi Dominus Sabaoth]], that is, of hosts, or of powers, especially the heavenly ones: of whom the angels cry: [[Is 6:3|Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of hosts|Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus exercituum]]. According to Jerome, for *Sabaoth* the Seventy put *Almighty*. With whom it seems to agree that John in the Apocalypse, bringing in the words of Isaias, says: [[Apoc 4:8|they rested not day and night, saying: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God Almighty|Requiem non habebant, dicentia: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus omnipotens]]. So, [[9:29|Unless the Lord of Sabbath had left us a seed|Nisi Dominus Sabaoth reliquisset nobis semen]], us Jews, that is, a remnant believing in Christ, namely the holy Apostles and the others converted from Judaism, of whom it is said through the Prophet: [[Is 61:9|these are the seed which the Lord hath blessed|Isti sunt semen cui benedixit Dominus]]; [[9:29|we had been made as Sodom and we had been like unto Gomorrha|sicut Sodoma facti essemus, et sicut Gomorrha similes fuissemus]], that is, we should have been utterly damned for our unbelief, as the inhabitants of Sodom and Gomorrha perished[[Gen 19:24||]], with the inhabitants of three other cities, namely Adama, Seboim and Segor[[Deut 29:23||]]. A certain writer explains these words of Isaias literally of the Jews not slain by the king of the Assyrians in the time of Ezechias. But such an explanation is rejected for the same reasons as the preceding one.

paras.t: Movet præterea Apostolus dubium, omni admiratione dignissimum. Quid ergo dicemus? id est, quum ex verbis Isaiæ jam pateat, paucos Judæorum credidisse, et multos de gentibus, quod mirum apparet, quid ergo dicemus ad hoc? scilicet: Quod gentes quæ non sectabantur justitiam, id est gentiles idololatriæ dediti, non observantes justitias legis divinæ seu scriptæ, apprehenderunt, id est, consecuti sunt, justitiam: justitiam autem quæ ex fide est, id est justitiam evangelicæ legis, quæ salvat per fidem, non justitiam legis Mosaicæ. Israel vero, id est populus Judæorum, sectando legem, id est præceptum, justitiæ, quæ in cærimoniis et sacrificiis consistebat, vel legem Moysis; vel, Legem justitiæ veræ et christianæ sectando, id est aliqualiter imitando, non quia lex Christi præcessit, sed quia prænuntiata et declarata est eis aliquo modo per Prophetas, sicque cœperunt eam sequi, præstolando eam, et secundum eam aliquo modo vivendo; in legem justitiæ veræ et christianæ non pervenit, recipiendo gratiam Christi, per quam evangelica adimpletur justitia, de qua dicit Salvator: Nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum. Quare sic contigit?
paras.en: The Apostle further raises a question most worthy of all wonder. [[9:30|What then shall we say?|Quid ergo dicemus?]] that is, since it is now plain from the words of Isaias that few of the Jews believed and many of the Gentiles, which seems wonderful, what then shall we say to this? namely: [[9:30|That the Gentiles who followed not after justice|Quod gentes quæ non sectabantur justitiam]], that is, the Gentiles given to idolatry, not keeping the justices of the divine or written law, [[9:30|have attained to justice|apprehenderunt justitiam]], that is, have obtained it: [[9:30|even the justice that is of faith|justitiam autem quæ ex fide est]], that is, the justice of the law of the Gospel, which saves by faith, not the justice of the law of Moses. [[9:31|But Israel, by following after the law of justice|Israel vero, sectando legem justitiæ]], *Israel*, that is, the people of the Jews, *following after the law*, that is, the precept, *of justice*, which consisted in ceremonies and sacrifices, or the law of Moses; or, following after the law of true and Christian justice, that is, imitating it in some way, not because the law of Christ went before, but because it was in some way foretold and made known to them through the Prophets, and so they began to follow it, waiting for it and in some way living according to it; [[9:31|is not come unto the law of justice|in legem justitiæ non pervenit]], of true and Christian justice, by receiving the grace of Christ, through which the justice of the Gospel is fulfilled, of which the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:20|unless your justice abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]]. [[9:32|Why so?|Quare]] did it so come about?

paras.t: Et respondet Apostolus: Quia non ex fide, sed quasi ex operibus, id est, Judæi quærebant justificari, non virtute et merito fidei Christi, sed per opera legis scriptæ, quum tamen sine fide et gratia Christi, nemo unquam salvari potuerit, sicut ostensum est. Offenderunt enim, id est impegerunt, in lapidem offensionis, id est in Christum, qui bonus est lapis salutis, impiis autem est lapis offensionis. Quemadmodum enim tendens in via, et pede in lapidem impingens, impeditur seu retardatur in via a progressu ad terminum viæ; sic Judæi peccando per infidelitatem atque præsumptionem, in Christum impingentes, retrusi atque impediti sunt a via salutis, nec pervenerunt ad finem beatum. Dicitur autem Christus lapis, propter constantiæ firmitatem. Sicut scriptum est apud Isaiam: Ecce pono in Sion, id est in populo Judæorum, inter quos conversatus est Christus; vel in Jerusalem, et in templo ubi frequenter fuit et docuit; lapidem offensionis et petram scandali, id est Christum: qui occasionaliter factus est Judæis lapis offensionis, id est peccati, quoniam contempserunt blasphemaveruntque eum, quemadmodum Petrus ait in Actibus: Hic est lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus. Factus quoque est eis petra scandali, id est spiritualis ruinæ. Sæpe enim Judæi scandalizabantur in verbis atque operibus Christi, non tamen nisi ex sua mera perversitate, dicentes: Ecce homo vorax, potator vini, amicus publicanorum, et multa hujusmodi. Et omnis qui crediderit in eum fide per dilectionem operante, non confundetur in æternum, nec spe sua frustrabitur; sed honorificabit eum Christus, quum fuerit suo tribunali oblatus.
paras.en: And the Apostle answers: [[9:32|Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were of works|Quia non ex fide, sed quasi ex operibus]], that is, the Jews sought to be justified not by the power and merit of faith in Christ, but through the works of the written law, although without faith and the grace of Christ no one could ever be saved, as has been shown. [[9:32|For they stumbled at the stumblingstone|offenderunt enim in lapidem offensionis]], *stumbled*, that is, struck against, *the stumblingstone*, that is, Christ, who to the good is the stone of salvation, but to the wicked a stone of stumbling[[Is 8:14||]][[1 Pet 2:7||]]. For as one going on a road and striking his foot against a stone is hindered or held back on the road from going on to the end of it, so the Jews, sinning by unbelief and presumption, striking against Christ, were thrust back and hindered from the way of salvation, and did not come to the blessed end. Christ is called a stone because of the firmness of his constancy. [[9:33|As it is written|Sicut scriptum est]], in Isaias[[Is 28:16||]]: [[9:33|Behold I lay in Sion|Ecce pono in Sion]], that is, among the people of the Jews, among whom Christ lived; or in Jerusalem and in the temple, where he often was and taught; [[9:33|a stumbling-stone and a rock of scandal|lapidem offensionis et petram scandali]], that is, Christ: who was made, as the occasion, a stone of stumbling, that is, of sin, to the Jews, since they despised and blasphemed him, as Peter says in the Acts: [[Acts 4:11|This is the stone which was rejected by you the builders|Hic est lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus]][[Matt 21:42||]]. He was made to them also a rock of scandal, that is, of spiritual ruin. For the Jews were often scandalized at the words and works of Christ, though only from their own sheer perversity, saying: [[Matt 11:19|Behold a man that is a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of publicans|Ecce homo vorax, potator vini, amicus publicanorum]], and many such things. [[9:33|And whosoever believeth in him shall not be confounded|et omnis qui credit in eum, non confundetur]], with faith that works by charity, shall not be confounded for ever, nor be cheated of his hope; but Christ will honour him when he is brought before his judgement seat.

paras.t: Hanc etiam scripturam allegat Petrus in prima sua Canonica, dicens: Propter quod continet Scriptura: Ecce ponam in Sion lapidem summum, angularem. Quod vero Petrus et Paulus adjecerunt, Qui crediderit in eum non confundetur, secundum translationem Septuaginta interpretum allegatur. Loco cujus, translatio nostra sic habet: Qui crediderit, non festinet. — Hic est lapis, qui juxta Danielis oraculum, exscissus est de monte sine manibus. De quo scriptum est per Zachariam: Super lapidem unum oculi septem sunt: quia in Christo fuerunt septem dona Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: Peter too alleges this scripture in his first Canonical Epistle, saying: [[1 Pet 2:6|Wherefore it is said in the scripture: Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone|Propter quod continet Scriptura: Ecce ponam in Sion lapidem summum, angularem]]. What Peter and Paul added, [[1 Pet 2:6|he that shall believe in him shall not be confounded|Qui crediderit in eum non confundetur]], is alleged according to the translation of the Seventy. In place of which our translation has: [[Is 28:16|He that believeth, let him not hasten|Qui crediderit, non festinet]]. This is the stone which, according to the oracle of Daniel, [[Dan 2:34|was cut out of a mountain without hands|exscissus est de monte sine manibus]]. Of which it is written through Zacharias: [[Zach 3:9|upon one stone there are seven eyes|Super lapidem unum oculi septem sunt]]: for in Christ were the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Apoc 5:6||]].
